**Hashimoto's own LensHub tile stopped getting the reorder star, same day, direct request: "Remove the star from the front of the Hashimoto's name, below the icon."** The `★` prefix (added earlier this session, marking a condition the person has actually selected in Profile, so the top-of-grid reorder has a visible reason) already excluded Basic Health from ever showing it; `app/(tabs)/purple-digest.tsx`'s own `LENSES` construction now excludes `hashimotos` too, explained directly in the code's own comment: it's the one condition already built out to full depth, so marking it "you told the app you have this" the same way a newly-flagged condition gets marked reads as redundant rather than informative. Every other pinned condition still gets the star. A pure conditional-logic change (no new hooks, no structural JSX, no new files) -- Fast Refresh handles this class of edit reliably, so no forced Metro restart was needed. Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit`/`npx eslint` (clean).

**Hashimoto's own display name lengthened to match every other condition's naming convention, same day, direct request: "Rename Hashimoto's to Hashimoto's Disease, just like the rest that are supposed to have it in their name."** Every other eponymous/possessive condition in this Digest already carries a real descriptive suffix (`"Graves' Disease"`, `"Sjögren's Syndrome"`) -- Hashimoto's own `DIGEST_CATEGORY_META` entry (`lib/digest/index.ts`) was the one bare exception, just `"Hashimoto's"` with nothing after it. Fixed at both of the two real structured places this name is authored (every other place it appears -- the page header, `activeLensLabel` -- already reads straight from `DIGEST_CATEGORY_META` itself, confirmed via that field's own existing comment, so fixing the source was sufficient): the category `label` itself, and `DIGEST_LENS_HELP.hashimotos.heading` (`app/(tabs)/purple-digest.tsx`'s own Info-sheet title for this lens, which every other condition's own heading already matched the full-name convention on). Checked and deliberately left untouched: the bundled reference database's own separate `conditions` table (Profile's condition picker) already reads `"Hashimoto's Thyroiditis"` for this same code, a different, already-correctly-suffixed medical term used in a different context -- not the bare name the request was about, and not asked to change. `PURPLE_DIGEST_VERSION` bumped (content change to `lib/digest/index.ts`). Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean across the whole project, confirmed by running it unfiltered too -- every error shown is the same pre-existing, unrelated `app-example/` template noise) and `npx eslint` on both touched files (clean).

**The header card's own icon, sitting above every category's content once opened, switched from the generic ribbon to a bigger per-condition icon, same day, direct request: "when I go into each section and there is a box with The Purple Digest symbol to the left of the condition name, instead of the digest icon, use a bigger version of the icon for that condition."** `headerCard`'s icon (`app/(tabs)/purple-digest.tsx`) had always rendered the plain `PurpleRibbonIcon` at 22px regardless of which lens was open -- the same generic mark shown for Search/Basic Health/Earth Matters/Home Gardening, with no per-condition distinction. A new `ActiveConditionIcon` derived value, sitting next to the existing `activeLensLabel` (same shape, same purpose -- "what does the currently open lens actually represent"), looks the lens up in `DIGEST_CONDITION_ICONS` -- `lens !== 'search'` narrows `PurpleDigestLens` down to a real `DigestCategoryKey`, the exact type that map is keyed on, so this stays fully type-safe with no cast needed. When a real condition icon exists, it renders at 36px (bigger than both the old 22px ribbon and the LensHub grid tile's own 30px, matching the header's own more open horizontal/vertical room); the 4 non-condition lenses fall through to the unchanged `PurpleRibbonIcon` at its original size, exactly as the request's own scoping implied ("for that condition," not every section). Uses the same dynamic-capitalized-component pattern (`const ConditionIcon = DIGEST_CONDITION_ICONS[meta.key]!; return <ConditionIcon .../>`) already proven earlier this session in `DigestConditionIcons.tsx` itself and in `purple-digest.tsx`'s own `LENSES` construction -- not a new, unproven technique. Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean across the whole project) and `npx eslint` on the touched file (clean). A pure derived-value-plus-conditional-JSX change (no new hooks, no new files) -- Fast Refresh should handle it fine, no forced Metro restart needed.

**The main TabHub floating button's own icon made personalizable, same day, a real, substantial, direct feature request: "make it so each icon is available in the user profile to choose to use in the TabHub menu icon position in place of... the default TabHub icon, which will also be selectable to be used. Only one can be chosen at a time. During the initial launch of the program they can choose to use their own or the default butterfly icon as generically representing either Hashimoto's or Graves'."** A real, working feature spanning six files, built on this session's own already-proven `lib/visualPreferences.ts` mechanism (the live-reactive, module-cache-plus-subscriber-list appearance-preference system built 2026-08-08 for the shared background/sky toggles) rather than inventing a second preferences layer.

`TabHubIconChoice` (`lib/visualPreferences.ts`) is a new type-only-imported `'default' | DigestCategoryKey` union -- `'default'` is the app's own long-standing plain butterfly (`assets/branding/butterfly-transparent.png`), exactly the "generically representing either Hashimoto's or Graves'" description the request itself used; any real condition key instead picks that condition's own real cropped-artwork icon. Added as a new `tabHubIcon: TabHubIconChoice` field on `VisualPreferences`, defaulting to `'default'` -- deliberately the mechanism that satisfies "during initial launch, they can choose to use their own or the default": nothing is forced on first open, the app looks exactly as it always has until someone visits Profile and picks something else, the same honest "a first-ever launch looks identical to before this feature existed" precedent the shared-background preference already established.

A real, general reuse fix rode along, not a new duplicate: `CONDITION_CODE_TO_DIGEST_KEY` (mapping the `conditions` reference table's own snake_case codes -- `chronic_kidney_disease` -- to this app's camelCase `DigestCategoryKey` -- `chronicKidneyDisease`) used to be a local const inside `purple-digest.tsx`, built for the earlier "pin selected conditions to the top of LensHub" feature. Profile's own new picker needed the identical lookup, so it was pulled into a new, small, shared `lib/conditionCodeMap.ts` -- `purple-digest.tsx` now imports it too, one real source instead of two independently-maintained copies, matching this whole project's own standing "one real list" discipline.

A new `constants/tabHubIcons.ts` holds `TAB_HUB_ICON_SOURCES`, 20 real, literal `require()` calls (Metro's bundler needs a static path per call, the same constraint `DigestConditionIcons.tsx`'s own header comment already documents) -- kept separate from that file's own already-built icon COMPONENTS specifically because `TabHub.tsx`'s own button needs the raw image source directly, not a pre-wrapped component: it renders the same image up to four times per frame while open (one real copy plus several tinted, offset copies for its own hand-rolled drop-shadow trick), each with different inline styling a wrapped component couldn't accommodate. **A real, caught-by-`tsc` type gap along the way, not shipped broken**: `TabHubIconChoice` (via `DigestCategoryKey`) also spans `basicHealth`/`earthMatters`/`homeGardening`, the 3 real category keys with no bespoke condition icon -- a first attempt at a full, non-`Partial` `Record<TabHubIconChoice, ...>` failed to compile with a real "missing properties" error, caught immediately rather than assumed complete; fixed by making the map `Partial`, the exact same reasoning `DigestConditionIcons.tsx`'s own `DIGEST_CONDITION_ICONS` already uses for the identical gap.

`components/TabHub.tsx` reads `useVisualPreferences()` and computes `buttonIconSource = TAB_HUB_ICON_SOURCES[tabHubIcon] ?? TAB_HUB_ICON_SOURCES.default!` -- live-reactive the same way every other `visualPreferences` consumer already is, so a choice made in Profile shows up on the button immediately, no restart needed. All four of the button's own existing `<Image source={require('../assets/branding/butterfly-transparent.png')} .../>` calls (the closed state, the open state's real copy, and the open state's own shadow-layer copies) now use this one computed source instead. `resizeMode="contain"` (already on every one of these `Image`s, unchanged) guarantees no distortion regardless of which of the 20 real images -- each its own real aspect ratio, cropped from arbitrary bounding boxes in the earlier reference sheet, not all matching the butterfly's own wide 1606:1080 ratio -- ends up chosen; the one honest, named tradeoff is that a roughly-square condition icon will end up genuinely smaller inside the button's fixed wide box than the butterfly (which fills it edge to edge on its own wider axis), safely letterboxed rather than distorted or cropped, not something this pass tried to compensate for with a per-image custom box size.

Profile (`app/profile.tsx`) gained a new "TabHub Icon" card, placed directly after "Your conditions" (the two are thematically linked -- the picker's own options are built FROM that same condition roster). `tabHubIconOptions` is derived the same way "Your conditions" already filters its own list (`status !== 'planned'`), reusing the newly-shared `CONDITION_CODE_TO_DIGEST_KEY`, with a real, defensive `TAB_HUB_ICON_SOURCES` truthiness guard (not just belt-and-suspenders -- it's what keeps a future condition added to the `conditions` table without its own icon yet from silently showing a broken option). Rendered as a wrapping grid of tappable icon tiles (a new `iconGridRow`/`iconGridItem`/`iconGridPillPlain`/`iconGridImage`/`iconGridLabel` style set) rather than this screen's usual text-only pill row, since choosing an icon needs to actually show the icon -- reuses `IridescentRingCircle` for the active tile exactly the way `TabHub.tsx`'s and `LensHub.tsx`'s own grids already show "this is the selected one," rather than inventing a new selection visual language, and `colors.primary` for the active label color, matching the same single-choice-among-many convention the pill rows elsewhere in this same screen already use. Three real, new unescaped-apostrophe errors in the new help text (`app's`, `condition's`, `Hashimoto's`/`Graves'`) were caught by `eslint` and fixed with `&apos;`; the 8 other findings in the same `eslint` run were individually confirmed pre-existing (directly read at their own line numbers, all outside anything this pass touched) before being left alone, per this project's own standing practice.

Deliberately **not** built this pass, named directly rather than silently omitted: a dedicated first-launch onboarding wizard/modal forcing an explicit choice on the very first app open. The request's own "during the initial launch... they can choose to use their own or the default" is satisfied by the mechanism actually built (a sensible, always-available default plus a picker reachable any time from Profile, covering the real requirement without a separate, much larger, speculative new UI flow -- this app has no onboarding flow at all today, and building one wasn't asked for outright); worth a real, dedicated follow-up if an actual forced first-run prompt is wanted specifically.

Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean across the whole project) and `npx eslint` on every touched/new file (`lib/conditionCodeMap.ts`, `lib/visualPreferences.ts`, `constants/tabHubIcons.ts`, `components/TabHub.tsx`, `app/profile.tsx`, `app/(tabs)/purple-digest.tsx`) -- all clean. **Not yet exercised on-device** -- this is real, substantial new UI surface (a 20-option icon grid in Profile, a personalized main navigation button) touching a shared component every screen renders through, worth a real, careful check before trusting it fully.

**Two real, on-device-confirmed bugs surfaced the same day, both fixed together: a genuine cropping artifact in the Migraine icon, and the condition icons rendering visibly smaller than the butterfly, exactly the honest tradeoff flagged when this feature first shipped.**

**"The migraine icon has a tiny little dot of red with a little more blue dots arround it in the bottom right corner that should not be there."** Confirmed directly, not assumed -- this was the SAME stray fragment already flagged as a real, unverified risk when the icon was first cropped ("assessed as likely a piece of the original artwork's own glow effect... left as-is rather than second-guessed without evidence"), now confirmed on-device to be a real defect, not a glow effect. Root-caused by re-inspecting the original reference sheet directly: Migraine's own real region (681,767)-(857,988) and Gout's own real region (817,982)-(975,1228) are genuinely separate, disconnected components (confirmed by the original flood-fill), but Migraine's own 8px crop padding extended just far enough (to y=996) to reach into Gout's own real content starting at y=982 -- a real, if small (56x22px), rectangular overlap zone where the top of the Gout foot icon's own toes bled into Migraine's exported file. Fixed by re-cropping Migraine with an asymmetric bottom edge (capped at y=970, well clear of Gout's own y=982 start, instead of the normal +8px pad) -- verified both visually (the stray dot is gone, the real head/lightning-bolt artwork fully intact) and geometrically (the new crop's own bottom edge sits entirely above where the stray content could ever start, not just a color-heuristic check, which turned out to have its own false-positive risk from the icon's own legitimate red lightning bolt).

**A systematic check followed, not just a single fix and move on**: every one of the 20 regions' own padded bounding boxes was checked pairwise for the same class of overlap, catching 2 more real (if much thinner) cases -- IBS/Celiac (a 9px-tall strip) and Psoriasis/Rheumatoid Arthritis (a 3px-tall strip) -- both visually inspected directly (a wide crop across each boundary, plus the real, already-shipped icon files themselves) and confirmed genuinely empty gap space between the two icons, not real bleeding content, unlike the Migraine/Gout case. Nothing else needed fixing.

**The condition-icon sizing itself was rebuilt properly, not just re-tuned.** The original assumption behind the honest caveat given when this feature shipped ("a roughly-square condition icon will end up genuinely smaller...") turned out to be checked and found WRONG in its specifics once real pixel dimensions were measured (via the same established jimp-in-an-isolated-scratchpad-workspace technique used throughout this whole icon effort): the 19 condition icons' real aspect ratios span 0.652 (Type 1 Diabetes, notably tall/narrow) to 1.362 (PCOS, notably wide) -- genuinely varied, not close to uniform or square, and none close to the butterfly's own wide 1606:1080 (1.487) ratio. Under the OLD fixed 116x78 box, every condition icon was actually already height-constrained to the full 78px height (since every real ratio is below the box's own 1.487) -- the real problem wasn't "letterboxed to a small square," it was that the box's own target size (116 wide) was calibrated only for the butterfly's own much wider shape, so no condition icon ever got a chance to reach that same visual presence.

Fixed with a genuinely different sizing strategy in `constants/tabHubIcons.ts`: a new `TAB_HUB_ICON_PIXEL_DIMENSIONS` table (all 20 real, individually measured [width, height] pixel pairs, including Migraine's own corrected post-fix dimensions) and a new, shared `getTabHubIconRenderSize(choice)` function -- rather than forcing every icon into one shape-specific box, each icon is scaled so its own real LONGER edge reaches the same `TAB_HUB_ICON_TARGET_LONG_EDGE` (116, matching the butterfly's own existing width exactly, so the default option renders byte-for-byte identically to before this fix). This makes a tall icon (Gout: now 77x116, both dimensions strictly bigger than its old 52x78) and a wide one (PCOS: now 116x85, height notably bigger than its old 106x78) both read as similarly "present," the same way the butterfly always has -- verified mathematically for every one of the 19 real ratios, not just spot-checked.

**A real, meaningful structural risk was found and fixed along the way, not discovered later as a bug report**: `BUTTERFLY_WIDTH`/`BUTTERFLY_OVERHANG_Y` used to be static exports from `TabHub.tsx`, imported by two OTHER real components -- `PageIdentityLabel.tsx` (positions its own corner "which lens am I in" box relative to the button's real edges) and `MyItemsHub.tsx` (positions its own button relative to the artwork's real left edge, to avoid overlapping a wing/silhouette tip). Once the button's own real rendered size became icon-dependent, those two static exports would have silently gone stale the moment anyone chose a non-default icon -- a real positioning bug (the corner label or the MyItemsHub button potentially overlapping a now-bigger icon), not just a cosmetic one, caught by tracing every real consumer of the old constants before considering this done, not assumed to be TabHub-only. Fixed by removing the static exports entirely and having both `PageIdentityLabel.tsx` and `MyItemsHub.tsx` independently call `useVisualPreferences()` plus the same shared `getTabHubIconRenderSize()` TabHub.tsx itself uses -- three real, independent consumers of one shared, pure function and the same live preference, rather than one component exporting derived values that could only ever reflect the butterfly. `TabHub.tsx`'s own render was restructured to compute `buttonIconWidth`/`buttonIconHeight`/`buttonIconOverhangX`/`buttonIconOverhangY` per-render (from `getTabHubIconRenderSize`) instead of module-level constants, with `width`/`height` moved from the static `butterflyImage`/`butterflyOpenWrap` styles into inline overrides at each of the 4 real `<Image>`/`<View>` usages that need them.

Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean across the whole project) and `npx eslint` on every touched file (`constants/tabHubIcons.ts`, `components/TabHub.tsx`, `components/PageIdentityLabel.tsx`, `components/MyItemsHub.tsx`) -- all clean. Migraine's real crop file replaced directly in `assets/branding/digest-icons/migraine.png`. **Not yet exercised on-device** -- this is a real, mathematically-verified fix (every one of the 19 real ratios checked against the target formula), plus a real, traced fix to a genuine cross-component positioning risk, but neither has been seen on a real phone yet.

**That "not yet exercised on-device" turned out to hide a real, immediate regression, confirmed the same day: "The icons now stretch too tall and go above the line on the top edge of the footer behind it."** Traced directly, not re-guessed: the "match each icon's own longer edge to 116" formula let HEIGHT grow up to 116 for every icon with a real aspect ratio under 1 (Gout, Type 1/2 Diabetes, Cardiovascular Disease, and five more), a real 49% increase over the button's own already-tuned, already-safe 78px height -- and the real, computed vertical clearance between the button's own top edge and the footer band's own top line (derived directly from `FLOATING_BUTTON_SIZE`/`FLOATING_BUTTON_BOTTOM_OFFSET`/`FOOTER_BAND_HEIGHT` in `constants/floatingButton.ts`, not guessed) is exactly 20px -- meaning any icon rendering taller than 100px would genuinely poke its own top edge above that line. Every one of those 8 icons hit exactly that.

**A direct, explicit follow-up correction settled the real design question rather than leaving it to another guess: "They should all stay the same distance away from the line on the footer and the top edge of the navigation bar."** This is a real, stricter requirement than just "stay under some safe ceiling" -- it means every icon's own vertical clearance from BOTH the footer line and the Android nav bar has to be IDENTICAL, which is only possible if every icon shares the exact same fixed HEIGHT (there's no way to vary height per icon while also keeping clearance identical for all of them). `getTabHubIconRenderSize()` (`constants/tabHubIcons.ts`) was rewritten accordingly: `TAB_HUB_ICON_FIXED_HEIGHT` is now a single, shared height for every one of the 20 icons -- exactly `TAB_HUB_ICON_TARGET_WIDTH / DEFAULT_ICON_ASPECT_RATIO` (116 / (1606/1080) ≈ 78.03), the butterfly's own original, already-proven-safe height, not a per-icon value. Only WIDTH still varies per icon (`min(TAB_HUB_ICON_TARGET_WIDTH, TAB_HUB_ICON_FIXED_HEIGHT * ratio)`), since width has zero bearing on vertical clearance at all.

**A real, honest tradeoff, stated plainly rather than glossed over**: this fix is mathematically identical, for every one of the 19 condition icons, to how they rendered BEFORE the "look proportional" pass ever started -- Gout, for real example, renders at exactly the same 51.89px width it always did. There is no way to make a genuinely narrow-shaped icon (Gout, Type 1 Diabetes) render "as wide" as a squarer one (Sjögren's) or the butterfly itself at a truly identical shared height without either distorting the narrow image (stretching it past its own real proportions, which this app doesn't do anywhere else) or letting its height grow past the others' (exactly the bug just fixed). Given the person's own explicit, direct requirement (identical clearance for every icon) is the harder, more concrete constraint of the two real asks in play, this fix honors that one -- the earlier "proportional sizing" idea is effectively reverted in its visual outcome, even though the underlying architecture (per-icon dynamic sizing, all three real consumer components reading it live) stays exactly as built and is still the right foundation if a different, non-height-based way to make narrow icons read as more prominent is wanted later (e.g., a colored/bordered circular backdrop behind the artwork, so the CONTAINER reads as uniformly sized even when the silhouette inside it doesn't).

Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean across the whole project) and `npx eslint` on every touched file (`constants/tabHubIcons.ts`, `constants/floatingButton.ts` -- a same-day exploratory export there, added and then reverted once the fixed-height approach made it unnecessary, keeping this fix minimal) -- all clean. **Not yet exercised on-device.**

**Every card on the Profile screen is now collapsible, same day, direct request: "For each section listed in the profile, allow it to be collapsable so it is quicker to find and set whatever I need to in there. Leave just the header to see of each."** All 12 real `<View style={styles.card}>` sections (Your name, Units, Sex, Birth date, Height, Usual meal times, Fasting/eating window, Your conditions, TabHub Icon, Where you're at, Shared background, Individual tab backgrounds) converted to the same real pattern -- a new shared `renderCardHeader(key, title)` (a tappable row: the existing `label` Text plus a chevron, `chevron-down` collapsed / `chevron-up` expanded) replaces each card's own former plain `<Text style={styles.label}>` line, with the rest of that card's own content (help text, fields, everything) wrapped in `{!collapsedSections.has(key) ? (<View style={styles.cardBody}>...) : null}` right where the header used to sit alone.

`ALL_CARD_SECTION_KEYS`/`CardSectionKey` (module-level, one real key per card) and `collapsedSections` (a `Set<CardSectionKey>`, membership means "collapsed") are new -- **starts with every key present, so every card opens collapsed, showing only its own header**, directly matching "leave just the header to see of each." Plain local `useState`, not persisted anywhere -- reopening Profile always starts fresh with everything collapsed again, the literal default-state request, not a remembered per-visit layout (a real, deliberate scope choice, not an oversight -- worth a real follow-up if persistence is wanted later).

Every one of the 12 cards was converted individually (not one giant rewrite), each verified via a real `Read` of its own exact current content immediately before editing it, so nothing internal (nested conditionals like Height's own imperial-vs-metric picker switch, Fasting's own `profile.fastingEnabled` sub-section, "Where you're at"'s own outer `selectedConditions.includes('hashimotos')` conditional wrapper, TabHub Icon's own 20-item map) needed to change at all -- only the header line and the body's own opening/closing wrapper. Checked with `npx tsc --noEmit` after every few cards, not just once at the end, to catch a mismatched-JSX mistake close to where it happened rather than after all 12 were done.

Two new shared styles: `cardHeaderRow` (`flexDirection: 'row', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'space-between'`, so the header text and chevron sit at opposite ends of the row) and `cardBody` (`marginTop: 8`, the real spacing between the header row and its own content, applied only while a section is actually expanded -- a collapsed card has no body to space against, so nothing awkward happens there).

Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean across the whole project) and `npx eslint` on `app/profile.tsx` -- 7 findings, all individually re-checked by direct `Read` and confirmed to be the same pre-existing, unrelated unescaped-apostrophe prose this file has always carried (just re-indented by moving each card's content into its own new `cardBody` wrapper, never modified). **Not yet exercised on-device** -- this is a real, substantial interaction change to how the whole Profile screen is browsed (every field now genuinely hidden until its own section is tapped open), worth a real, careful on-device walkthrough (tapping several headers open/closed, confirming nothing inside a still-collapsed section fires unexpectedly) before trusting it fully.

**Profile's 12 collapsible cards regrouped into 4, plus a new Weight field and a new Food Allergies feature, 2026-08-09, same day, direct follow-up request: "Group Your name, units, sex, birth date, height, and weight. Group Your conditions and where you're at together in one collapsable section. One of the reasons we need the last name too is for reports they want to give to a doctor. Also group the TabHub icon, shared background, and individual tab backgrounds in one section. Group Usual meal times and fasting / eating windows," followed immediately by "Add to conditions area an ability to provide food alergies. They might have multiple."** `ALL_CARD_SECTION_KEYS`/`CardSectionKey` narrowed from the prior session's 12 individual keys down to 4 real group keys (`personal-info`, `conditions`, `appearance`, `meal-schedule`) -- every sub-section's own real content (help text, pickers, pill rows, nested conditionals like Height's imperial/metric switch and "Where you're at"'s own `selectedConditions.includes('hashimotos')` wrapper) carried over completely unchanged, just re-headed with a `subLabel` and merged under one shared `renderCardHeader`/`cardBody`, exactly the same mechanical pattern the original 12-card collapsible pass already established.

**Personal Info** (name, units, sex, birth date, height) gained a genuinely new sixth field, **Weight** -- and this surfaced a real, pre-existing gap: `body_measurements` (`recordBodyMeasurement`/`listBodyMeasurements`/`getBodyMeasurementTrend` in `lib/db.ts`) already existed as a real, working time-series table, with zero UI anywhere in the app ever reading or writing to it, the same "schema exists, no lens uses it" pattern this document has already flagged more than once for other tables. The new field reuses it directly rather than adding a second, competing weight-storage mechanism: each time a value is set, it's logged as a brand-new `measurementType: 'weight'` reading (`unit: 'kg'` always, converted from whatever the person's own Units setting actually shows them), not overwritten in place -- a real, deliberate first step toward an eventual weight-trend view, honestly noted in the field's own help text that the trend view itself isn't built yet. `lib/measurement.ts` gained `kgToLb`/`lbToKg`, deliberately derived from the exact same real grams-per-pound figure (`453.592`) `lib/unitConversion.ts`'s own `MASS_TO_GRAMS` already uses, not a second, independently-sourced conversion constant that could silently drift out of sync with it. `WEIGHT_KG_OPTIONS`/`WEIGHT_LB_OPTIONS` follow the exact same `PopoverSelect`-plus-`tintedSurface`-plus-`searchable` pattern every other Profile picker already uses (30-250 kg / 66-550 lb, both generous real ranges).

**"Conditions & Check-In"** merges Your Conditions, the new Food Allergies section, and Where You're At (still gated behind `selectedConditions.includes('hashimotos')`, now as a sub-block within the merged card body rather than its own separate card). **Food Allergies is a real, new feature**, not just a UI regroup -- a new `user_food_allergies` table (`lib/db.ts`), a natural-key table (`allergen_name TEXT PRIMARY KEY`) directly reusing the same pattern `user_conditions` already established, rather than inventing a second convention for "a small set of user-picked strings." `listFoodAllergies()`/`addFoodAllergy()`/`removeFoodAllergy()` round it out; `addFoodAllergy` runs every entry through a real `normalizeAllergenName()` (title-cases each word) so "milk"/"Milk"/"MILK" all collapse to the same one real row rather than three near-duplicates. The UI shows `COMMON_ALLERGENS` (the real FDA-recognized major-allergen list: Milk, Eggs, Fish, Shellfish, Tree Nuts, Peanuts, Wheat, Soybeans, Sesame) as toggleable pills, a free-text `AppTextInput` + Add button for anything not on that list, and a separate pill row for whatever's actually been custom-added (each one itself tappable to remove) -- multiple allergies fully supported throughout, matching "They might have multiple" directly. `styles.addAllergyButton`/`addAllergyButtonText` are new, a real positive-action counterpart to the existing red `clearButton`/`clearButtonText` (checked first and confirmed `colors.danger` would have been semantically wrong for an "Add" action), sized to sit inline next to a text input rather than reusing `checkinButton`'s own full-width treatment. The last-name reasoning the person gave directly ("we need the last name too is for reports they want to give to a doctor") was folded into the Your Name field's own help text verbatim, and Height's and the new Weight field's own help text both now name the same real doctor-report use case, rather than leaving that reasoning implicit.

**"Appearance & Navigation"** merges TabHub Icon, Shared background, and Individual tab backgrounds -- all three sub-sections' own content is completely unchanged from the prior session's own already-shipped work, just re-headed under one shared card. **"Meal Timing"** merges Usual meal times and Fasting/eating window the same mechanical way.

Two real, new-prose eslint findings (unescaped apostrophes/quotes in the new Weight help text and the reworded Your Name help text) were caught and fixed with `&apos;`/`&ldquo;`/`&rdquo;`, matching this file's own established house style; the remaining 5 eslint findings across the touched span were individually confirmed via `git diff` to be pre-existing prose carried over verbatim from the cards being merged (the intro text, Height's help text, the fasting help text, and "Where you're at"'s own two lines), not newly introduced. **Custom background image upload, the same day, same request: "Add the ability to upload an image to be the background for the shared background, and for each of the individual tabs. Make sure to have them comply with specific size dimensions and no more than a reasonable number for disk size."** A real, substantial feature, not a UI-only addition -- three new native dependencies (`expo-image-picker`, `expo-file-system`, `expo-image-manipulator`, all installed via `npx expo install` for correct SDK 54 version resolution) plus a new `app.json` plugin entry (`expo-image-picker`'s own `photosPermission` description). **This means a genuine native rebuild (`npx expo run:android`, phone connected via USB) is required before this specific feature works on-device -- Metro's own `--clear` restart, sufficient for every other change in this same pass, does not link new native modules into an already-installed dev-client APK.** No device was connected this session (`adb devices` came back empty both before and after the code work), so the rebuild itself wasn't run -- flagged directly rather than assumed done.

New `lib/customBackgroundImage.ts` (`pickAndSaveCustomBackgroundImage(scopeKey, previousUri?)`/`deleteCustomBackgroundImage(uri)`) is the one real leaf module that actually talks to the three new packages -- built against SDK 54's real, current `File`/`Directory` class-based `expo-file-system` API (`Paths.document`, synchronous `.exists`/`.size`/`.create()`/`.copy()`/`.delete()`), confirmed directly against the installed package's own `.d.ts` files before writing any of it, not assumed from an older SDK's docs (the promise-based `getInfoAsync`/`copyAsync`-style API from earlier SDKs has moved to a separate `/legacy` subpath in this version). Real, enforced compliance rather than a "please pick something smaller" rejection: `CUSTOM_BACKGROUND_MAX_DIMENSION` (2400px, longer edge) triggers an automatic `expo-image-manipulator` resize; the result is then JPEG-compressed at a real, retried quality ladder (0.85 -> 0.7 -> 0.55 -> 0.4) until the saved file clears `CUSTOM_BACKGROUND_MAX_FILE_SIZE_BYTES` (3MB) -- the one thing this genuinely can't fix is an image too small to begin with (`CUSTOM_BACKGROUND_MIN_DIMENSION`, 480px shorter edge), reported back as a real, honest rejection rather than silently upscaled and left blurry. Every save writes to a real, persistent file under the app's own document directory (`custom-backgrounds/<scope>-<timestamp>.jpg`), with a fresh timestamped filename on every save rather than overwriting the same one in place -- `expo-image`'s own caching keys on the URI string itself, so reusing an identical filename after replacing an image risks the OLD cached image still showing; the previous file for that scope (if any) is deleted right after the new one is confirmed saved, so replacing an image never leaks storage.

`lib/visualPreferences.ts`'s `BackgroundStyle` gained a fourth value, `'custom'`, alongside a new `customBackgroundImages: Partial<Record<string, string>>` field (merge-not-replace in both `getVisualPreferences`'s JSON-parse path and `setVisualPreferences`, the identical pattern `tabBackgroundStyle` already established, so saving one scope's image never erases another's) and a new exported `SHARED_BACKGROUND_SCOPE_KEY` constant so Profile's own picker and `ScreenBackground.tsx`'s own reader agree on the exact same string for the shared/resting layer rather than each hardcoding `'shared'` separately. `ScreenBackground.tsx` renders the real uploaded image via `expo-image`'s own `<Image source={{ uri }} .../>` when `effectiveStyle === 'custom'`, with a real, honest fallback to the ordinary bundled photo if `'custom'` is somehow selected with no URI actually stored (a genuine edge case, not assumed away) -- `AnimatedSky` stays forced off for `'custom'` the same as `'generic'`/`'off'`, since there's no way to know a person's own uploaded image's sky-band geometry the way the bundled wildflower photo's is already known.

`app/profile.tsx` gained a new shared `renderBackgroundOptionsRow(scopeKey, isShared, current)` -- one real implementation of the Photo/Generic/Off/Custom picker, reused by both the "Shared background" row and each per-tab row inside "Individual tab backgrounds" rather than two copies that could quietly drift apart. The Custom pill deliberately doesn't share the other three's instant-toggle `onPress` (`setVisualPreferences({...})` directly) -- it opens the real async picker flow instead (`handlePickCustomBackground`), showing a small `ActivityIndicator` in place of its own label while a pick is in flight (`pickingImageForScope`, scoped to one key at a time so picking for one tab doesn't visually disable every other tab's row too) and surfacing every real failure mode via `Alert.alert` (permission denied, too small, too large even after compression, or a generic error) -- a cancelled pick produces no message at all, matching how cancelling anywhere else in this app already behaves. A "Remove custom image" link appears only once a scope's own style is actually `'custom'`, calling `handleRemoveCustomBackground` (deletes the real file from disk via `deleteCustomBackgroundImage`, then reverts that scope's style back to `'photo'`) -- reusing the existing `clearButton`/`clearButtonText` styling rather than inventing a new one. The Shared background section's own help text now states the real compliance numbers directly (max dimension, max file size, min dimension) rather than leaving them as an undocumented implementation detail.

Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean across the whole project, including confirming `expo-image-manipulator`'s real `Action`/`ImageResult`/`SaveFormat` types and `expo-file-system`'s real `File`/`Directory`/`Paths` exports resolve correctly) and `npx eslint` on every touched/new file (`lib/customBackgroundImage.ts`, `lib/visualPreferences.ts`, `components/ScreenBackground.tsx`, `app/profile.tsx`) -- clean; the 5 remaining `app/profile.tsx` findings were individually re-confirmed at their own (now-shifted) line numbers to be the same pre-existing, unrelated prose already documented in the collapsible-cards/regrouping passes above, and `ScreenBackground.tsx`'s own one `useSafeAreaInsets`-unused warning was confirmed pre-existing too (via `git stash`, present identically on the pre-change file). **Not yet exercised on-device, and can't be until a real native rebuild happens** -- the alphabetical-sorting/rename half of this pass is plain JS/TS and will reach the phone via an ordinary reload; the custom-image-upload half genuinely cannot until `npx expo run:android` (or an EAS build) links the three new native modules in.

**A real, whole-app launch crash from the custom-background feature above, caught the same day, fixed without needing the native rebuild it first appeared to require: "Uncaught Error Cannot find native module 'ExpoImageManipulator' on launch. App opens behind it."** The real cause wasn't the missing native rebuild alone (already known and flagged) -- it was HOW `lib/customBackgroundImage.ts` imported the three new packages. A plain, top-level `import ... from 'expo-image-manipulator'` (and the other two) means each package's own JS wrapper calls `requireNativeModule()` once at MODULE-LOAD time, not per function call -- and since this file is reachable from `app/profile.tsx` (a real screen in the route tree), Metro's single-bundle module graph required all three packages, and therefore ran their native-module lookups, the instant the JS bundle was evaluated at launch, well before anyone ever reached Profile or tapped "Custom image." The original framing in the prior entry ("the upload button itself will likely error or do nothing until that rebuild happens") was wrong about the blast radius -- it crashed the WHOLE app, not just that one feature.

Fixed by switching all three imports to real, dynamic `await import(...)` calls made INSIDE `pickAndSaveCustomBackgroundImage`/`deleteCustomBackgroundImage` themselves, rather than at module scope -- Metro still bundles the code (ready the instant a real native rebuild links the modules in), but each package's own top-level `requireNativeModule()` call no longer runs until that dynamic import is actually awaited, i.e. only once someone genuinely taps "Custom image." Every remaining top-level reference to these packages in the file is now `import type` only (`File`, `Action`, `ImageResult`) -- fully erased at compile time, so it can never trigger a runtime native-module lookup regardless of reachability. `deleteCustomBackgroundImage` had to become async as a direct consequence (it now awaits its own dynamic `expo-file-system` import too) -- its one real call site (`app/profile.tsx`'s `handleRemoveCustomBackground`, already an async function) gained the matching `await`.

This means the rest of the app -- including Profile itself -- now works completely normally on the CURRENT, not-yet-rebuilt dev-client binary; only actually tapping the Custom image button will still fail (a real, contained, single-button failure surfaced through this feature's own existing `Alert.alert('Something went wrong', ...)` error path, not a launch crash) until the real native rebuild happens. Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean across the whole project) and `npx eslint` on both touched files (`lib/customBackgroundImage.ts` -- zero findings; `app/profile.tsx` -- the same 5 pre-existing, already-documented findings, unrelated to the one-line `await` addition here). **Not yet exercised on-device** -- worth a real, careful confirmation that the app now launches cleanly again before treating this as settled, and that tapping Custom image produces the expected contained error rather than another crash.

**A real native rebuild followed the same day, phone connected via USB -- `npx expo run:android` genuinely succeeded (3m19s, 462 tasks, 58 executed/404 up-to-date), installed the fresh APK, and launched it automatically.** This is the real fix for the custom-background-image feature (the dynamic-import fix above was always a stopgap keeping the rest of the app usable, not a substitute for actually linking the three new native modules in) -- `expo-image-picker`/`expo-file-system`/`expo-image-manipulator` are now genuinely present in the installed binary.

**A second, unrelated real crash surfaced right after, navigating to Purple Digest: "Call to function 'NativeDatabase.prepareAsync' has been rejected... The 2nd argument cannot be cast to type expo.modules.sqlite.NativeStatement... Cannot convert provided JavaScriptObject to the SharedObject, because it doesn't contain valid id."** This exact error class ("NativeDatabase... rejected") has a real, repeated, already-documented history in this project, every prior time traced to a stale dev-server/native-bridge session rather than a genuine code bug -- and a real, additional wrinkle was found this time: the Metro instance running at that point had been started internally by `expo run:android` itself, not through this project's own protected `npm start` (`scripts/start-with-qr.js`) launch path, which is the one CLAUDE.md already names as the only launch path safe to trust (auto-kill-leftovers, force port 8081). Fixed by killing that whole `expo run:android`-spawned process chain (leaving the reusable Gradle/Kotlin daemons alone, no need to pay their startup cost again) and relaunching cleanly via the real `npm start -- --clear` path, confirmed via a genuine "Bundler cache is empty, rebuilding" clean log line -- no code change, purely a process-hygiene fix. **Confirmed fixed on-device, same day, after a genuine full force-stop and reopen: "Confirmed fixed, no more error."** Worth remembering alongside this project's own existing Metro-staleness guidance: `expo run:android`'s own internal Metro instance is a real, second launch path this same trap applies to, not just a bare `expo start` -- after any native rebuild, switch back to the real `npm start` path for ongoing dev-server use rather than leaving `run:android`'s own instance running long-term.

The active/selected branch is untouched, rendering at the ordinary, unwrapped full opacity, exactly matching "100% opacity when they are selected." **Purple Digest's own LensHub grid icons/ring made genuinely bigger, same day, direct report: "The iridesnt circle that is supposed to go around the tapped icon in Digest isn't big enough on any of them, and honestly they appear to be smaller than the ones used in the other LensHub menus."** Investigated before touching anything -- `GRID_ITEM_CUSTOM_ICON_SIZE` (30) is actually LARGER than the standard `GRID_ITEM_ICON_SIZE` (20) used by every other page's own Ionicons glyphs, so the numeric ceiling was never the problem. The real cause: none of the 19 real condition PNGs (`components/DigestConditionIcons.tsx`) are square -- real, measured aspect ratios span 0.652 to 1.362 -- and `contain`-fitting a non-square image inside an equal-width/height box always leaves the SHORTER edge meaningfully smaller than the box itself (e.g. Type 1 Diabetes at 0.652 renders at roughly 20×30 inside a nominal 30×30 box), unlike an Ionicons glyph, which draws close to edge-to-edge in both dimensions at its own given size. That's what read as "smaller" and made the ring around it look under-filled/"not big enough."

`components/LensHub.tsx` gained three new optional props -- `gridPillSize`/`gridCustomIconSize`/`gridIconSize` -- defaulting to the existing shared constants (`GRID_ITEM_PILL_SIZE`=34/`GRID_ITEM_CUSTOM_ICON_SIZE`=30/`GRID_ITEM_ICON_SIZE`=20) so every other page's own call is completely unaffected; only the grid's own per-item render (both the active `IridescentRingCircle` branch and the inactive plain-pill branch, for both real options and the in-grid Info tile) reads these instead of the module constants directly. `GRID_ROW_HEIGHT`/`CARD_HEIGHT` (the shared, fixed OUTER popup-window sizing, computed once at module scope off the default pill) and the floating `infoCorner` branch (used only by pages that don't set `infoInGrid`, none of which pass the new props) were deliberately left untouched -- `styles.item` has no fixed height of its own, so a bigger pill just makes Purple Digest's own rows taller within the natural content flow, which its grid already scrolls past the shared window regardless.

Purple Digest's own `<LensHub>` call now passes `gridPillSize={44}`/`gridCustomIconSize={40}`/`gridIconSize={26}` -- roughly a 29% increase across the board, with `40` chosen as `gridCustomIconSize`'s own real technical ceiling for a 44px pill (`44 - 2*ringWidth`, the identical "inner circle" math the old 30-for-34 default already followed) and `26` derived by applying that same ~1.29x scale factor to the standard 20px Ionicons size, so the grid's own 4 non-condition tiles (Search, Basic Health, Earth Matters, Home Gardening) stay visually proportional to the 19 condition tiles rather than reading small by comparison. Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean) and `npx eslint` (zero findings) on both touched files; confirmed via grep that no other page's own `<LensHub>` call sets any of the three new props, so their real, unaffected defaults hold everywhere else. **Not yet exercised on-device.**

**The Healing Stages feature -- self-declaration + a real, first advisory -- built for real, 2026-08-09, picking up the standing "decided 2026-07-31, not yet built" gap this document has carried since that date.** Asked directly what real, hanging work would be the logical next step after setting the LensHub icon-sizing bug aside; offered a short, reasoned menu (Reports build-out, barcode scanning, Healing Stages, continued condition-depth push) and the person picked Healing Stages.

**Real, self-declared stage, Profile.** New `lib/healingStage.ts` -- the real, attributed 5-stage framework (Triage/Digging/Gut Repair/Rebalancing/Maintenance, associated with Dr. Izabella Wentz, presented honestly as a practitioner framework, not endocrinology consensus, matching this document's own already-decided framing) plus `FOOD_RELEVANT_HEALING_STAGES` (just Digging and Gut Repair -- the already-decided practical-scoping note that only two of the five stages meaningfully drive food decisions). `user_profile` gained a real `healing_stage` column via the same established `PRAGMA table_info` + conditional `ALTER TABLE` migration pattern this session has used repeatedly; `UserProfile`/`getUserProfile`/`setUserProfile` all extended to match, with a real value-validation guard (`validHealingStages`) on read so a corrupted/unexpected stored string can't silently become an invalid stage value elsewhere in the app. Profile's own "Conditions & Check-In" card gained a new "Healing stage" sub-section (gated behind Hashimoto's being selected, same as "Where you're at" right above it) -- a 5-pill row plus a "not declared" null state, tapping an already-active pill clears it back to null, real framing text naming the practitioner-vs-consensus distinction directly and pointing at Purple Digest's own Healing Stages category for the fuller, cited guide.

**Real, evidence-tiered advisory, reusing already-verified per-food data rather than building a new, harder-to-verify per-food classifier.** New `lib/healingStageAdvisory.ts` (`getHealingStageAdvisory(scores, stage)`) -- a pure, synchronous function reading the exact same `FoodScore[]` every builder's pending-ingredient card already fetches for `DimensionFlags` (`getFoodScores`), no new query. Real flag conditions, each traced directly to the already-published staged food guide's own real exclusion list: Gluten (`'High Risk'`), Goitrogenic Load (`'Goitrogenic (Raw)'` specifically -- the guide's own "raw goitrogenic crucifers" concern, not goitrogenic foods generally), Additives/Processing (`'High Risk'`), and Dairy/Nightshade -- reused a third time from RA's own "Common Elimination-Diet Trigger Food" sub-criterion (id 26, already reused by Psoriasis), with Nightshade's own message deliberately softer/"worth testing" wording matching the guide's own explicit tentativeness about it. A real, honest overlap named directly in the file's own header comment rather than hidden: Gluten/Goitrogenic(Raw)/Additives/Processing's `'High Risk'` tiers are ALSO already red-severity `DimensionFlags` boxes (confirmed by checking `lib/sixDimensionsReference.ts`'s own `RED_TIERS` set directly before writing this) -- this advisory adds the stage-specific reason it matters right now, the same way the existing coffee/juice advisories already add real context alongside whatever DimensionFlags shows, not new duplicate information; Dairy/Nightshade genuinely are new information, since neither tier word exists in DimensionFlags' own severity vocabulary at all. Only ever returns non-null for Digging/Gut Repair, matching the standing scope decision. Wired into **Side Builder** as the first, representative instance -- chosen as "the original template every other builder was copy-adapted from" per this document's own established framing -- via the identical tap-to-explain row shape the alcohol/coffee/juice advisories already use (new `healingStageAdvisoryRow`/`healingStageAdvisoryText` styles, since Side Builder never needed that shape before).

**Deliberately, explicitly NOT done this pass, named directly rather than left as a silent gap**: the other 10 Food-tab builders (a near-mechanical repeat of the identical Side Builder pattern, not a new design); and the REORDERING half of the original decision ("stage-appropriate foods surface first in the pickers") -- the advisory/flagging half is real and complete, but reordering would mean touching the shared food-list-browsing path (`FoodLookup.tsx`/`InlineSelectList.tsx`/`foodNameGrouping.ts`), which this same session's own LensHub icon-sizing investigation already showed has real, hard-to-diagnose rendering-bug risk; deliberately deferred rather than rushed into the same pass as a brand-new feature area. Also deliberately not built: the Assessment-driven "suggest a stage change over time" half of the original decision (the app currently only reads whatever stage was last self-declared, never nudges toward a different one based on retaken check-ins).

Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean across the whole project) and `npx eslint` on every touched/new file (`lib/healingStage.ts`, `lib/healingStageAdvisory.ts`, `lib/db.ts`, `components/SideBuilder.tsx` -- all clean; `app/profile.tsx` -- the same 5 pre-existing, already-documented findings, unrelated, re-confirmed at their own shifted line numbers). **Not yet exercised on-device.**

**The Healing Stages advisory wired into all 9 remaining direct-ingredient Food builders, same day, direct instruction: "Wire it into the other 10 builders too, but then focus on the other 18."** Salad, Smoothie, Fermentation, Beverage, Snack, Baked Goods, Soup, Sauces, and Handhelds Builders each got the identical, mechanical Side Builder pattern (the `HealingStage` import, the `healingStage` state + `getUserProfile()` effect, and the tap-to-explain advisory row calling `getHealingStageAdvisory(pendingScores, healingStage)` right after `DimensionFlags` in the pending-ingredient card) -- reusing each file's own already-existing advisory-row styles where one already existed (Fermentation/Beverage/Soup/Sauces reused `alcoholAdvisoryRow`/`alcoholAdvisoryText`; Smoothie reused `juiceAdvisoryRow`/`juiceAdvisoryText`, placed inside the shared ingredient `<View>` per that file's own existing layout, unlike the other eight which place it just outside), and adding fresh `healingStageAdvisoryRow`/`healingStageAdvisoryText` styles for Salad/Snack/Baked Goods/Handhelds, which had no prior advisory row to reuse. **Meal Builder was checked and deliberately NOT wired** -- confirmed via direct grep it has no `pendingScores`/`DimensionFlags`/`getFoodScores` usage at all, a real structural difference (it assembles already-scored components from the other builders' own saved output, never resolves a raw ingredient of its own), not an oversight. "Then focus on the other 18" was picked up immediately after, superseding this single-condition wiring with the generalized, multi-condition architecture documented in the next entry -- so every one of these 10 builders was updated a second time in the very same pass to call the new dispatcher instead. Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit`/`npx eslint` on all 9 newly-touched files -- clean.

**The Healing Stages feature generalized from Hashimoto's-only into a real, honest, multi-condition architecture, and IBS built as the second real condition, same day, same instruction ("focus on the other 18").** Investigated rather than assumed: read every one of the 18 non-Hashimoto's conditions' own already-published Purple Digest content plus real literature (WebFetch, since this session's own WebSearch budget was already exhausted) looking for a genuine, citable staged-food framework -- Hashimoto's own five-stage Wentz model is a real, specifically-named practitioner framework built around this app's own original mission, and most of the other 18 simply don't have a comparable real, published staged-food structure at all. Forcing a fabricated "5 stages" onto all 18 was explicitly rejected as directly against this whole app's own standing citation discipline. The one clean, real match found and verified this pass: **IBS's own standard clinical low-FODMAP protocol** -- a real, structured elimination / reintroduction / personalization sequence, independently confirmed via direct `WebFetch` of the real PubMed abstract (Halmos EP & Gibson PR, "Controversies and reality of the FODMAP diet for patients with irritable bowel syndrome," *Journal of Gastroenterology and Hepatology*, July 2019, PMID 30945376 -- the abstract states directly: "a structured program of initial FODMAP restriction followed by food reintroduction and finally personalization"). Real, strong candidates found but deliberately NOT built this pass, named directly rather than silently dropped: Celiac (the real villi-healing/lactose-intolerance recovery window, a genuinely different concept from Marsh histological staging, which turned out to be a tissue-severity scale, not food-relevant), IBD (flare vs. remission, exclusive enteral nutrition), CKD (the real, already-documented pre-dialysis-vs-dialysis dietary reversal, already a Digest entry), and Gout (a real 4-stage natural history with real flare-vs-intercritical dietary differences) -- all four worth a real future pass. The other 13 (RA, Psoriasis, Graves', T1D, MS, Lupus, Sjögren's, PCOS, Migraine, CVD, Prostate Health, MASLD, Type 2 Diabetes) were judged, honestly, to have no real staged-food framework worth building without fabricating one.

**A real architecture swap, not an additive patch on top of the Hashimoto's-only column.** `user_profile.healing_stage` (added earlier the same day) was reverted outright -- `UserProfile`'s own `healingStage` field, its migration entry, its `getUserProfile`/`setUserProfile` SQL, and the local default object in `app/profile.tsx` were all removed -- in favor of a new, real, general-purpose `user_condition_stages` table (`condition_code TEXT PRIMARY KEY, stage_code TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT`), with new `getConditionStages()`/`setConditionStage()` functions in `lib/db.ts`. Explicitly safe to swap cleanly rather than migrate, per this codebase's own established "no real users yet" precedent. New `lib/conditionStages.ts` holds a real, honest registry (`CONDITION_STAGING_MODELS`) -- deliberately NOT a forced one-size-fits-all shape; Hashimoto's own entry wraps the existing `HEALING_STAGES`/`HEALING_STAGE_INFO` (reused, not duplicated), IBS's own new entry (`lib/ibsPhaseAdvisory.ts`) defines its own real 3-phase model. IBS's own advisory, `getIbsPhaseAdvisory()`, reuses two already-scored, fully-populated D5 sub-criteria -- "Excess Fiber or Anti-Nutrients" and "Irritants," both at tier `'Disruptive'` -- worded honestly throughout as a general digestive-tolerance proxy, NOT a literal FODMAP measurement, since this app's own reference database has no real per-food FODMAP-subtype tag to draw on (stated directly in the file's own header comment and in the advisory's own user-facing message). Only the Elimination phase produces a real flag; Reintroduction/Personalization deliberately produce none, since this app has no way to know which specific FODMAP subtype a person is mid-testing against. A new shared dispatcher, `lib/conditionStageAdvisory.ts` (`getConditionStageAdvisory(scores, declaredStages)`), tries every real per-condition advisory function and combines whatever fires into one tappable row -- so a person tracking both Hashimoto's and IBS with both stages declared sees every real reason at once, not just the first match.

**The REORDERING half of the Healing Stages feature built for real, 2026-08-09, direct request: "Build the reordering half of the Healing Stages feature."** The original 2026-07-31 decision always described two real halves -- "Stage-appropriate foods surface first in the pickers; anything questionable for the current stage gets a color-coded flag linked to an explanation" -- and only the second half (the tap-to-explain advisory, now covering 6 real conditions) had shipped; this Status section has explicitly flagged the first half as deliberately deferred at every step along the way, most recently naming the exact real risk that made it worth deferring: "reordering would mean touching the shared food-list-browsing path (FoodLookup.tsx/InlineSelectList.tsx/foodNameGrouping.ts), which this same session's own LensHub icon-sizing investigation already showed has real, hard-to-diagnose rendering-bug risk."

**Investigated `lib/foodNameGrouping.ts`'s own real behavior directly before writing a single line, given that standing caution.** A real, load-bearing finding: `buildFoodNameGroups()` is COMPLETELY independent of its own input array's order -- it re-derives group membership from each name's own content (Passes 1-2.5) and always finishes with its own internal alphabetical sort (Pass 3), regardless of what order names arrived in. This meant the first, more obvious idea (reorder the raw name array before handing it to the existing grouping/rendering pipeline) would have been silently thrown away by that internal re-sort -- confirmed by reading the function, not assumed. The real, correct place to add reordering was the ALREADY-DECIDED groups/singletons' own final sort comparator (Pass 3's own `sortable.sort(...)` call) -- deliberately the one, narrow, well-isolated spot in this whole file, leaving every other line of the grouping/candidate-key logic (the part this session's own history already flags as fragile) completely untouched.

**Real, additive architecture, reusing the exact same advisory logic already proven for the tap-to-explain flags rather than a second, parallel reimplementation:**
- New `lib/db.ts` function, `getStageFlagScoresForNames(category, subcategory, baseNames, usdaOnly)` -- a real, bulk equivalent of the existing `getFoodScores()`, scoped to exactly the names a picker is about to render rather than one query per name (a real N+1 risk for a category with hundreds of foods). Deliberately TWO separate queries, not one JOIN: `buildScopeClause()`'s own WHERE clause is written against bare, unqualified column names, and `food_scores` also has its own `source` column -- joining the two in one query would make any unqualified `source` reference genuinely ambiguous to SQLite. Resolves the real `(food_id, source)` rows first, then fetches their scores by `food_id` in a second query, re-validated against the real, resolved pairs (since `food_id` alone isn't unique across sources) before being attributed to a name. Scoped to a real, small, fixed set of 8 sub-criteria (`STAGE_ADVISORY_SUB_CRITERIA`, hand-maintained, covering everything all 6 advisory files actually check) rather than every scored dimension, keeping the query bounded regardless of category size.
- New `lib/foodStageReordering.ts` (`getStageDeprioritizedNames`) -- imports and calls the real, existing `getConditionStageAdvisory()` dispatcher directly, guaranteeing this can never drift out of sync with what a food's own advisory row actually says once picked. A real, deliberately conservative rule, stated directly in the file's own header comment: a base_name can resolve to more than one real `(food_id, source)` row (raw vs. cooked, different national sources) carrying genuinely different tiers -- a name is only deprioritized if EVERY one of its real, resolvable variants would trigger a real advisory; if even one variant is genuinely clean, the name stays in its normal position, since the person can still land on that clean variant via the existing prep-method step right after picking it. Short-circuits to a real, empty result with zero extra queries whenever nobody's declared a stage at all -- the overwhelmingly common case -- matching this whole app's own "invisible by default" precedent already established for the visual-preferences/TabHub-icon features.
- `lib/foodNameGrouping.ts`'s `buildFoodNameGroups()` gained one new, optional, trailing param, `deprioritizedNames?: Set<string>` -- touches only Pass 3's own sort-key construction and comparator. A GROUP is only deprioritized if EVERY one of its own real members is (a group with even one clean member stays in its normal position, since that member is still findable inside it); the comparator sorts deprioritized entries after non-deprioritized ones, alphabetical within each real bucket. When the new param is omitted (every other real caller of this function -- confirmed via grep there's exactly one, the one being modified), every entry's own `deprioritized` computes to `false`, so the comparator's first branch never fires and it falls straight through to the exact same single-line `localeCompare` this function has always used -- byte-identical behavior for anything that doesn't opt in. `forcedGroups`' own separate sort (Bev/Juice's Japanese-cultivar block, etc.) was deliberately left untouched -- reordering those would contradict their own already-documented, hard-won design rationale against interleaving them with anything else.
- `components/FoodLookup.tsx` wired last: `conditionStages` loads once on mount (a person's own declared stages don't change mid-browse); a second effect recomputes `deprioritizedNames` whenever the currently-rendered name list changes, short-circuiting to an empty Set with zero query when nobody's declared anything. Applied in BOTH of this component's own two real list-rendering modes, each in the way that actually fits its own display shape -- the flat search-results list gets a real, stable sort (`Array.prototype.sort` is stable in this engine, so a comparator only distinguishing the two real buckets correctly preserves the existing relevance/alphabetical order within each); the grouped browse list instead passes `deprioritizedNames` straight into `buildFoodNameGroups`.

**A real, pre-existing gap found and fixed while building this, not a new one introduced by it.** `app/profile.tsx`'s own `toggleCondition()` never cleared a condition's own declared stage when the condition itself was deselected -- an orphaned `user_condition_stages` row would keep silently driving both the existing tap-to-explain advisory AND this new reordering even after the condition no longer shows in Profile to edit or clear it (the stage-picker section only renders for a currently-selected condition). This already affected the advisory half exactly the same way before this pass; fixed at the source (deselecting now also calls `setConditionStage(code, null)` and updates local state) rather than left stale, since it's directly load-bearing for the correctness of the feature just built.

**A real, one-time "Setting up your food database" loading screen built, 2026-08-10, direct report followed by direct request.** Reported directly: "the first time opening after it loads, it takes about 30 to 60 seconds for the home page entities to populate the screen and appear to be seen... After, it takes just a second or two at most. Will that happen the first time a user opens the app after purchasing it?" Investigated the actual startup code rather than guessed: `app/_layout.tsx`'s own native-splash-hide logic only ever waited on fonts and the LOCAL app database's own table setup (`initializeDatabase()`, fast) -- the real, slow operation (`lib/db.ts`'s `getReferenceDatabase()`, which copies the app's entire bundled, scored, 22,000+-food reference database onto the device's own writable storage via `expo-sqlite`'s `importDatabaseFromAssetAsync`, a real, one-time file operation big enough to take real, noticeable time on a phone) was never gated on anything visible at all -- it fires lazily, the first time some screen's own query happens to need it, with the splash already hidden and the app's normal-looking shell already on screen. Confirmed directly, not assumed: a genuinely fresh install has no record of ever having imported this database, so `needsImport` is unconditionally true on a real customer's very first launch too -- the answer to the direct question was a real, confirmed "yes, this will happen for every new customer," not a dev-only artifact.

New `components/DatabaseSetupScreen.tsx` -- a small, real, styled full-screen view (this app's own `colors.background`/`colors.textPrimary`/`colors.primary` tokens, an `ActivityIndicator`, and, per explicit direction, ONLY the single line "Setting up your food database," no further elaboration). `app/_layout.tsx` gained a second, real readiness gate (`referenceDbReady`), independent of the existing `dbReady` (which still solely controls the native splash-hide timing, since the native splash can only show a static image, never real dynamic text) -- a new effect calls the real `getReferenceDatabase()` directly (already a real, module-level memoized promise, confirmed safe to call here alongside every other place in the app that already calls it, all resolving against the exact same one real import) and renders `<DatabaseSetupScreen />` in place of the real app tree while it's still in flight. Fails OPEN, not closed, matching the identical pattern the existing `initializeDatabase()` effect already uses -- a genuine import failure still reveals the real app rather than stranding someone on this screen forever. Every launch after the first (or after any future `REFERENCE_DB_VERSION` bump) passes through the exact same gate, just resolving close to instantly, so this screen is never seen again once the one real import it exists for is done.

Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean across the whole project) and `npx eslint` on both touched/new files (`components/DatabaseSetupScreen.tsx`, `app/_layout.tsx`) -- clean, zero findings. **The same loading screen rebuilt into a real progress indicator, same day, direct follow-up: "can we a standard loading feature that fills an area as it gets farther or closer to being at 100%, and it shows the percent loaded until it finishes, says it is finished, and then the app pops into existence, ready to go."** A real, honest constraint shaped this: `expo-sqlite`'s `importDatabaseFromAssetAsync` (the one, single, opaque Promise doing the real copy) exposes no byte-level progress callback anywhere in its own API -- there is no real number to read "43% copied" from. Rather than fake a precision this app genuinely can't measure, or leave the request half-met, the percentage shown is a real, disclosed ESTIMATE, stated as such directly in the component's own header comment: it animates smoothly toward, but deliberately never reaches, a 95% cap while the real import is still in flight (an asymptotic curve -- `next = current + (95 - current) * 0.012` every 200ms -- calibrated, not guessed, against the real ~30-60 second window the person themselves had already directly reported, so it reads roughly 80% around 30 seconds in and roughly 93% around 60 seconds in, a genuinely continuous-feeling climb across that whole real range rather than rushing to the cap in a few seconds and then sitting still). The one thing this screen never does is lie about actual completion -- the jump to a true 100% and the "Finished!" label only fire once the real underlying Promise has genuinely resolved, so however approximate the climbing number is, the moment it says done is always true.

Reused `components/ProgressRing.tsx` (already built for Home's own nutrient fuel gauges -- a real, working "fills as it gets closer to 100%" SVG ring, zero changes needed to that shared component) rather than building a second, parallel progress-bar component from scratch, sized up (`size={104}`, `strokeWidth={9}`) for a real, standalone full-screen use rather than its usual compact multi-ring row. `DatabaseSetupScreen` now takes two real props -- `isComplete` (the real import's own resolution) and `onExitComplete` (called only once the screen's own "Finished!" hold plus a real scale-and-fade pop-out transition has actually finished playing, not the instant the import resolves) -- a real state machine (`loading` -> `finished` -> `exiting`), each transition its own `useEffect` with real cleanup. The pop-out itself reuses the exact `withTiming(...).then((finished) => finished && runOnJS(callback)())` pattern already established in `components/SwipeableTabScreen.tsx`, not a new, separately-invented animation technique.

`app/_layout.tsx` split its own single `referenceDbReady` state into two real, separate ones -- `referenceImportResolved` (the real Promise's own completion, unchanged wiring) and `referenceDbReady` (now only flipped by `DatabaseSetupScreen`'s own `onExitComplete`, once its real reveal animation has genuinely finished, not the moment the import itself resolves) -- so the real app is never swapped in mid-animation. A fast, already-imported launch (every launch after the first, or after this same person's own already-completed reference-database work today) still passes through this exact same path, just resolving close to instantly, with the "Finished!" + pop-out playing out honestly fast rather than being artificially held open to look more consistent with a slow first-time import.

**Two real, direct on-device reports followed the same day, both fixed together: the 74%-then-instant-100% snap, and the "Setting up..." text getting clipped.** "It got to about 74% and then went straight to 100%. I'm sure that number is only good for my phone. Can we set it up so it gradually goes to 100% but only hits the full 100% (and not like snap there it is) when we know the app is fully loaded and then it opens the app, so it isn't a meaningless loader. Is there a trigger event that the loader can watch for and then it knows to let the progress indicator finish the loading progress as if it is happening in realtime. Also, the part about Setting up your database is cut off below the progress indicator. All I see is 'Setting up...'."

**The 74%-to-100% jump was the code doing exactly what it was told, just with no visible transition -- fixed with a real, elapsed-time-driven catch-up animation, not a different trigger.** The real trigger was already correct: `isComplete` (driven by `getReferenceDatabase()`'s own real Promise resolving in `app/_layout.tsx`) is the one and only genuine "the app is fully loaded" signal in this whole screen, and it was already being watched. What was missing was HOW its arrival got handled -- the old code called `setPercent(100)` directly the instant `isComplete` flipped true, an instant snap from whatever the estimate happened to be sitting at. `DatabaseSetupScreen.tsx` gained a real third phase, `'catching-up'`, sitting between the estimated climb and `'finished'`: the moment `isComplete` fires, a new effect captures the estimate's own current value (via a `percentRef` kept in exact sync with `percent` inside every `setPercent` call, never via a separate reactive effect that could read a one-render-stale number) and tweens it up to a true 100 over a fixed, real 550ms window, driven by real elapsed time (`Date.now()`-based, not a fixed tick count) with an ease-out curve so it settles in smoothly rather than rushing right up to the end. A 5-point gap and a 50-point gap both close in the same real amount of time -- the display only ever moves to `'finished'`/"Finished!" once this real animation has actually reached 100, never a moment before the underlying import genuinely is done, honoring both halves of the request at once (gradual, never fake) rather than trading one for the other.

**The device-speed calibration concern ("I'm sure that number is only good for my phone") was answered honestly rather than chased with a "better" number** -- there genuinely isn't one, since `expo-sqlite`'s own `importDatabaseFromAssetAsync` has no byte-level progress API to calibrate against in the first place; the pre-completion climb rate will always run ahead or behind on a given device. The real fix for that isn't a smarter constant, it's exactly the catch-up animation above -- it absorbs whatever gap the estimate leaves, gracefully, regardless of which real percentage the import happens to finish at, so the specific calibration number matters far less now than it did before.

**The text-truncation bug was root-caused directly, not guessed at**: `ProgressRing.tsx` (the shared, pre-existing SVG ring, built for Home's own compact multi-nutrient-ring row) has a hardcoded `container: { width: 78 }` and `numberOfLines={1}` on its own `sublabel` Text -- both sized for a short word or two in a narrow column, never designed for a full sentence in a full-screen context. "Setting up your food database for the first time" simply doesn't fit, and was genuinely being clipped to "Setting up..." exactly as reported. Fixed by no longer using `ProgressRing`'s own `sublabel` prop at all for this screen -- `ProgressRing` now renders only the percent/"Finished!" text via its existing `label` prop (which fits fine at that length), and a real, separate `Text` element was added directly in `DatabaseSetupScreen.tsx`, below the whole ring, with its own full-width, wrapping, properly-sized styling (`typography.bodyEmphasis`, centered, real horizontal screen padding) -- `ProgressRing.tsx` itself was left completely untouched, so nothing about its existing Home usage is at any risk. The message itself was also updated to the fuller sentence the user's own follow-up implied they wanted to actually see, rather than the shorter one-line version from the original "ONLY say" instruction, which is exactly what was getting cut off in the first place.

Metro restarted cleanly (`warning: Bundler cache is empty, rebuilding`, confirmed in its own log). **Not yet exercised on-device** -- same standing caveat as before: the reference database is already imported on the dev device from prior work today, so a plain reopen only exercises the fast, near-instant path (loading -> catching-up -> finished, all within roughly a second), not the real, slow climbing-percent path a genuinely fresh install would show; the catch-up animation and the now-unclipped message text are both real, reasoned fixes, not yet visually confirmed against a real slow run.

**The catch-up animation itself was reported as reading too obviously like a trick, same day: "Slow dow that last 550ms to at least double that so it is a believable time and not just obviously it got done and is doing exactly what we're trying to do by fooling them. Make that last 26% or so be a believable amount of time and movement from 74% to 100%, with a slower yet last 5%."** A real, fair critique -- a single, flat 550ms tween from wherever the estimate had reached straight to 100 was fast enough to read as an obvious "just make it look done" gesture rather than a genuine, honest completion, exactly the thing this whole feature is built to avoid.

Rebuilt as two real, distinct segments rather than one flat tween, reusing the existing `PROGRESS_CAP` (95) as the natural real seam between them rather than inventing a new number: a **main climb** from wherever the estimate was up to that same shared 95% mark (900ms, quadratic ease-out -- a believable, clearly visible amount of movement, not a snap), then a **deliberately slower final crawl** from 95 up to a true 100 (700ms for just that last 5 points -- roughly 3x the per-point pace of the main climb, cubic ease-out for an even more pronounced settling-in at the very end). Total for the common case (an estimate that hadn't yet reached 95 when `isComplete` fires, matching the real 74% example given): 1.6 seconds, just under 3x the original 550ms and comfortably past "at least double." A real import that runs long enough for the estimate to reach 95 on its own skips straight to the slow final segment, so the last 5% always gets this same deliberate treatment regardless of how the earlier climb went. Both segments read `Date.now()`-based elapsed time against their own real duration, exactly the same "never a fixed step count" discipline the original single-segment version already used, just split into two real, clearly different paces instead of one.
