Traced the real mechanism by hand rather than guessing at a download URL: fetched the page's own raw HTML/JS bundles directly via `curl`, found `slv.exportera.sparaHelaDatabasen()`'s real implementation (`slv.mvc.getUrlAction("HamtaHelaDatabasen","Spara")`, itself resolving to `slv.page.appFolder + "Spara/" + "HamtaHelaDatabasen"` = `/Spara/HamtaHelaDatabasen`), submitted via a hidden-iframe form POST with no body. Reproduced this directly: a bare `curl -X POST` hit a real `411 Length Required` (the server, a genuine Microsoft-IIS/ASP.NET stack, needs an explicit `Content-Length` even for an empty body); an explicit empty `--data ""` fixed it, returning a real `200 OK` with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=LivsmedelsDB_202608101841.xlsx` and a genuine 678,355-byte file. Verified as a real, non-corrupt XLSX before trusting it further -- confirmed the real `PK\x03\x04` ZIP magic bytes and a genuine internal worksheet structure (5.3MB `sheet1.xml`) via `unzip -l`, not just a successful-looking HTTP status.

**A real, 1,315-decision batch from the Reference Database Audit tool applied, 2026-08-10, same day, direct instruction: "Please go to [C:\Dev\Database Audit\inside-story-audit-decisions3.json] to apply the changes. **A real, tiered matching strategy, built and verified rather than a blind exact-key lookup.** Dumped every real, distinct `(category, subcategory, base_name)` triple currently in the live database via `sqlite3.exe -json`, then resolved each of the 1,315 decisions in three real tiers: (1) an exact match; (2) a same-category, base_name-unambiguous-within-that-category fallback, which correctly handled 269 real decisions that had been recorded with an empty subcategory before Meat later gained its own real "Meat & Poultry"/"Fish & Seafood" split -- safe because the category itself is still a known, exact match, never guessed; (3) a cross-category base_name-only fallback (never applied to move decisions, per this project's own established, repeated rule that guessing a move's FROM-category defeats the whole point) -- genuinely unneeded this pass, zero decisions required it. All 1,315 resolved; zero left unmatched.

**Two real bugs caught and fixed before any SQL was generated, not after.** First, case-insensitivity: the real schema's own `base_name TEXT COLLATE NOCASE` means SQL-level lookups are already case-insensitive, but a plain JS `Set`/`Map` is not -- 2 real decisions ("Pork belly," "Maple syrup") were silently failing to match their real, differently-cased live values ("Pork Belly," "Maple Syrup") until this was caught and every JS-side comparison was folded to lowercase (while still using the real, correctly-cased live value for the actual generated SQL). Second, a real statement-ordering bug: a move+rename combo needs the rename issued FIRST against the row's original `(category, subcategory, base_name)`, with every later statement (hide/unhide/move) then matching on the NEW base_name -- doing it the other way around would have left the move's own WHERE clause referencing a category/subcategory the row had already left.

**4 rename-only decisions (Halibut Fish, Herring Fish, Pork Liver, Salmon Fish) were genuinely ambiguous even within category="Meat" alone** -- each shares its own base_name with an unrelated, correctly-placed "Fish & Seafood" row by pure coincidence. Resolved with real verification, not a guess: each decision's own recorded `rowCount`/`sources` (e.g. "Halibut Fish": rowCount 2, sources USDA) was checked directly against the live database's real row-by-row breakdown per subcategory, and all 4 matched the "Meat & Poultry" subcategory specifically and exactly -- the same real "American Indian/Alaska Native Foods" catch-all leak this project already fixed once before for "Lingcod Fish" (see this document's own 2026-08-05 entry). Worth naming directly rather than silently expanding scope: the person's own recorded decisions were renames only, not moves -- these 4 rows stay in "Meat & Poultry," not reclassified to "Fish & Seafood," matching exactly what was actually decided, not what this session independently noticed as a related, adjacent opportunity.

Applying the rename already made these 3 unreachable by their old name (since the Set only matches a row's CURRENT base_name, and the new renamed value was never in it), but the 3 now-dead string entries were still removed from that Set for real cleanliness, not left as stale, unreachable artifacts -- matching this file's own established "remove dead code, don't leave it unreachable" precedent. The other two (Alcohol subcategory-pending-scan, Bev/Juice allowlist) had no real, currently-hit example to copy verbatim -- named directly rather than silently guessed as verbatim: these two are a reasoned reconstruction following the same established wording pattern, not a byte-exact replica, since the original generator script wasn't recoverable this session.

**The ABV/RS alcohol calculator, scoped and agreed 2026-08-03, was found to already be fully built as of 2026-08-10 -- discovered and documented 2026-08-11, since it had shipped only via an anonymous auto-checkpoint commit with no real commit message and no Status entry.** `lib/alcoholCalculator.ts` implements the real, agreed math directly: `calculateEthanolGrams()` (volume mL × ABV% × 0.789 ÷ 100), ethanol calories at 7 kcal/g (the Atwater general conversion factor), and residual-sugar calories at 4 kcal/g (never reduced by cooking retention, since sugar doesn't evaporate the way ethanol does -- only its concentration in a reduced dish changes, a separate question this calculator deliberately doesn't attempt). A real, cited cooking-retention table (`ALCOHOL_RETENTION_OPTIONS`, 9 real presets from "Not Cooked" through "Simmered/Baked, 2.5+ Hours") sources Augustin et al. 1992, *J Am Diet Assoc* (PMID 1556354) -- the actual original peer-reviewed study behind the retention percentages widely reproduced online, not just repeated from a secondary source. `components/AlcoholCalculator.tsx` (`AlcoholCalculatorPanel`) renders it as a real, inline expandable panel -- deliberately not a React Native `Modal`, since this app's own `OverlayContext` portal (what `PopoverSelect` needs for its own fields) can't paint above a separately-windowed native `Modal` on Android; an `Animated.View`/`LinearTransition` expand-in-place avoids that conflict entirely. Wired into exactly the four builders whose own category allowlist includes Alcohol -- Beverage, Fermentation, Soup, Sauces -- gated on the identical `isAlcoholicFood(pendingResolved)` check the existing alcohol advisory row already uses, sitting directly below it. Confirmed correctly scoped: beer is not offered here at all (matches the already-documented reasoning that real brewing chemistry means dextrins/starches survive fermentation as unfermented carbs an ABV/RS formula would systematically undercount), and this never overrides a food's own real, tracked reference-database values -- it's a standalone, informational estimate for the specific case a real bottle (an off-catalog proof, a homemade wine, a reduced sauce/soup) doesn't match any database row closely enough. Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint` on all four consumer files plus the two source files -- all clean.

**A companion, real Basic Health Digest entry followed the same day, prompted by the person sharing a fresh chemistry-and-metabolism reference document** (`metabolic_alcohol_formulas.md`) covering the same ABV/ethanol-mass math already implemented above, plus a real "Human Metabolic Pathway" section (liver first-pass, ADH/ALDH, and unsourced claims of "lipolysis inhibition up to 70%" and "gluconeogenesis suppression"). The real, precise numbers turned out to be two distinct figures, not one vague "up to 70%": a controlled human study (Siler et al. 1999, *American Journal of Clinical Nutrition*, PMID 10539756, isotope-tracer methodology, 24g alcohol dose) found adipose fat release (lipolysis) dropped 53% and whole-body fat oxidation dropped 73%, driven by a 2.5-fold rise in circulating acetate that directly suppresses lipolysis. A second, related study from the same research group (Siler et al. 1998, *American Journal of Physiology-Endocrinology and Metabolism*, PMID 9815011, 48g alcohol dose) found gluconeogenesis dropped 45% versus placebo over the 5 hours after drinking, via a real, different mechanism (an NADH/NAD+ shift that starves the pathway of what it needs). New entry `lifestyle-alcohol-liver-metabolism` (`lib/digest/lifestyleEnvironment.ts`), tagged `category: 'basicHealth'` -- deliberately not Hashimoto's-specific, since this is genuinely universal human physiology, matching this app's own already-corrected Basic Health scope rules (see that section's own 2026-08-08 entry) rather than siloed to one condition. Carries a real `DigestChart` (the two Siler 1999 figures, the only chart data this pass had a single defensible source for) and cross-links directly to the app's own alcohol calculator feature above, plus a reciprocal link from the existing `lifestyle-alcohol-advisory` (Hashimoto's-specific antibody research) entry. **A real repo-bloat problem was found and fixed the same day, discovered as a side effect of trying to push the day's own work.** `git push` (96 commits) hung past 9.5 minutes with no clear progress -- investigated rather than just retried with a longer timeout, and found `.git` had grown to 16GB. Root cause, confirmed via `git-filter-repo --analyze` (installed as a standalone script under `~/tools/`, not `pip install`, after a first `py -m pip install --user` attempt leaked a `Lib`/`Scripts` install into the project's own `lib`/`scripts` folders on Windows' case-insensitive filesystem -- caught and cleaned up immediately, no real damage): 11 stray `assets/data/foods_reference.db.bak-2026-08-11*` copies (~139MB each, all from the same day, already gone from disk and from HEAD but still sitting in history from before their own deletion commits) plus two stray `test_current_shape.db`/`test_alt_shape.db` files, and, the bigger problem, `unified-database/unified_foods.sqlite` (114MB, over GitHub's hard 100MB-per-blob push limit) never having been migrated to Git LFS the way `assets/data/foods_reference.db` already had been in an earlier session -- 21 separate commits each carrying a full new copy of it.

Also found and cleaned up along the way, unrelated to the size problem but blocking `git-filter-repo` from running at all: 8 stale, abandoned worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/agent-*` (leftover from earlier subagent `isolation: "worktree"` runs that should have auto-cleaned but hadn't), each holding only uncommitted, divergent `foods_reference.db` rebuild experiments branched from a commit already merged into `main` -- checked each one's own `git status` by hand before removing anything, confirmed nothing represented real, unique, committed work, then removed the worktrees and their now-pointless branches.

**Fixed with a real, careful history rewrite, not just a bigger timeout** -- a genuinely hard-to-reverse operation, done only after explicit confirmation and a full safety-net backup (`git bundle create ... --all`, verified via `git bundle verify` before touching anything). `git-filter-repo --path-glob 'assets/data/*.bak*' --invert-paths` (plus the two named test-db paths) stripped the junk from all 400 commits' history, dropping `.git/objects` from 1.1GB to 86MB in one pass. `git lfs migrate import --include="unified-database/unified_foods.sqlite" --everything` retroactively converted every historical version of that file into an LFS pointer, matching the treatment `foods_reference.db` already had. A real, easy-to-miss gotcha caught before trusting it: right after the LFS migration, `unified_foods.sqlite` sat in the working tree as a 134-byte pointer file, not real content (`git lfs ls-files` showing `-` rather than `*`) -- the real 114MB object was safely present in `.git/lfs/objects`, just not smudged into the checkout; fixed with `git lfs checkout`. Both databases' `PRAGMA integrity_check` passed `ok` after the full rewrite, and `npx tsc --noEmit` stayed clean, before anything was pushed.

`git-filter-repo` removes the `origin` remote as a safety measure by default -- re-added it, then force-pushed the rewritten history (every one of the 400 commits carries a new SHA now, unavoidable with this kind of rewrite). The push itself uploaded 87 LFS objects, 9.5GB total, then completed cleanly; a follow-up `git fetch` confirmed local `main` and `origin/main` match exactly. The local `.git` folder still shows ~17GB on disk afterward -- that's the local LFS object cache (already fully uploaded, safe to prune later via `git lfs prune` if disk space matters, not a functional problem either way). The full backup bundle from before the rewrite is kept at `../hashimotos-app-FULL-BACKUP-2026-08-11.bundle` (133MB) as a real, verified restore point, not deleted. **This was a real, one-time repo-hygiene fix, not a new standing workflow change** -- the two files that actually need LFS (`foods_reference.db`, `unified_foods.sqlite`) are both now correctly tracked via `.gitattributes`, so ordinary future rebuilds of either one will go through LFS automatically without needing this kind of intervention again; the real lesson worth carrying forward is to actually clean up (delete, not just leave for `.gitignore` to catch going forward) any stray multi-hundred-MB backup file the moment its own job is done, rather than letting it sit committed and then merely deleted in a later commit, which is what created this problem in the first place.

**The alcohol calculator became a real, tracked-value source, not just an informational estimate -- 2026-08-11, direct request, same day.** Reported directly: "There is no alcohol in the alcohol category or the beverage category, and Beverages is very sparce on choices, so I can't test the alcohol calculator" -- investigated and found, in sequence, two separate real issues rather than one: most of the apparent Bev/Alcohol sparseness turned out to be deliberate, individually-reviewed curation from the very same 1,315-decision audit batch documented above (cross-referenced exhaustively against all 3 real decision-export files, exact row-count matches everywhere, corrected on the record once confirmed -- "I was wrong to call this a bug"), with the real remaining blocker being Metro dev-server staleness (a 5-hour-old process spanning the exact moment `REFERENCE_DB_VERSION` was last bumped, fixed with a clean `npm start -- --clear` restart). A second, genuine crash followed immediately after that restart -- `no such column: needs_translation` -- root-caused to `lib/db.ts` still referencing a column from a same-day hand-translation effort that had already been deliberately reverted (the reference database was restored to its 2026-08-10 state per explicit prior instruction, excluding that translation work, since the separate Unified Whole-Foods Database project will eventually replace it properly) -- fixed by removing the two dead `AND needs_translation = 0` clauses from `buildScopeClause()`, confirmed working on-device ("Alcohol shows up now").

Once alcohol was actually reachable and testable, a real design gap surfaced directly: "I'm not sure why the quantity and units now have to be filled out and what they have to do with the alcohol now that I told the calculator how many ml ABV, residual sugar and cook time." At that point the calculator was purely informational -- a separate, standalone estimate shown alongside Quantity/Unit, never affecting what actually got tracked for the ingredient. The person's own follow-up named the real fix directly: "this is probably where the quantity should be to allow for more than 1 shot, or a 3 fl oz pour for many options, and remember that people aren't going to understand how this all works, so there needs to be a way to communicate it and make this easy." Confirmed via `AskUserQuestion` rather than assumed, given how much this changes: the calculator's own computed result should become the real, tracked value for the ingredient, replacing the plain reference-database-row-times-Quantity/Unit math entirely -- **"Yes -- calculator becomes the tracked value (Recommended)."**

**Built as a real, additive override layer, not a replacement of the existing per-food nutrient lookup.** Every one of the four builders whose own category allowlist includes Alcohol (Beverage, Fermentation, Soup, Sauces) got the identical treatment, each `_ingredients` table gaining 7 new nullable columns via the standard `PRAGMA table_info` + conditional `ALTER TABLE` migration pattern (`calculator_volume_ml`, `calculator_abv_percent`, `calculator_residual_sugar_g_per_l`, `calculator_retention_id`, `calculator_pours`, `calculator_calories`, `calculator_carbs_g`) -- null on every ordinary ingredient, exactly as before. A single shared type, `AlcoholCalculatorOverride` (renamed from an initial `BeverageCalculatorOverride` the moment its reuse across all four builders became clear, rather than let four near-identical types drift), carries the calculator's own real inputs (so a saved ingredient can restore the calculator to its original state) alongside the two derived totals actually used for tracking. Each builder's own `save`/`update` functions bind the same 7 fields; each builder's own `getXNutrientBreakdown` gained one new branch, checked first, right after the existing foodId/source resolution: when `calculatorCalories` is non-null, `itemTotals` is built directly from `{ energy_kcal: calories, carbohydrate: carbsG }` and the normal grams/food_nutrients lookup is skipped entirely for that one ingredient -- every OTHER nutrient (protein, fat, vitamins, minerals) is deliberately left at zero, matching this app's own already-cited research that distillation strips out virtually all non-ethanol content, and matching what the calculator was already scoped to estimate even in its original, purely-informational form. The 6-Dimensions breakdown functions are explicitly untouched -- D1-D6 scoring still reads the ingredient's own real foodId/source, unaffected by this override, since qualitative scoring and quantitative tracking are two genuinely different questions.

**A new Pours field closes the actual "more than 1 shot" gap named directly in the request.** `POURS_PRESETS` (`lib/alcoholCalculator.ts`) offers 1 through 12; Volume was relabeled "Volume (per pour)" so the relationship reads naturally, and the calculator's own math multiplies Volume x Pours into one real total (linear in volume, so an exact total across every pour, not an approximation layered on top) before computing ethanol/calories/sugar. The panel reports this upward reactively -- no separate "confirm" button, matching every other field here -- via a new `onOverrideChange(override, suggestedQuantity, suggestedUnit)` callback: a real, non-null override the instant Volume and ABV both resolve (Pours defaults to 1), `null` again the instant either gets cleared back out, with `suggestedQuantity`/`suggestedUnit` being the honest literal total in mL for the parent builder to auto-fill Quantity/Unit with, so nobody has to separately compute or type that number by hand.

**Real, plain-language communication built in at three separate points, directly answering "make it easy" rather than assuming the mechanism speaks for itself.** Every field gained an inline hint explaining what it actually means in ordinary language (ABV as "the % Alc/Vol printed on the bottle," residual sugar as "the natural sugar left over in the drink itself... close to zero in a dry wine or a plain spirit like vodka or whiskey," cook time as "if you're just pouring and drinking it... leave this at Not Cooked"). The result box gained a real, colored "Tracking this now, not the database's standard serving -- Quantity and Unit above have been updated to your real total" confirmation the instant a valid result exists. And a third, parent-side note appears directly above the Quantity/Unit fields themselves whenever the calculator is driving them, honestly describing the ACTUAL current behavior rather than a hoped-for one: Quantity/Unit stay fully editable by hand (no new `disabled` state was added to the shared `PopoverSelect` component in this pass, a real, deliberate scope boundary given how many other callers across the app depend on it), but the calories/carbs actually tracked keep coming from the calculator regardless of what gets picked there afterward -- the note says exactly that, pointing back at Volume/ABV/Pours as the real place to change the total, rather than implying a manual edit would silently revert to plain tracking when it currently does not.

**One real, deliberately named gap, not silently left unaddressed**: `BuilderFavoriteIngredient` (the shared JSON-snapshot shape every one of the ten sub-builders' own favoriting mechanism already writes to) doesn't carry any of the seven calculator fields -- reusing a favorite built from a calculator-tracked alcohol ingredient falls back to plain Quantity/Unit tracking (still the real total mL the calculator computed at save time, just no longer re-deriving calories/carbs from ABV/residual sugar). Deliberately not fixed this pass, to keep the work scoped to the four builders themselves rather than touching a type shared by every other builder's own favoriting path too -- worth a real, separate follow-up if favoriting a calculator-tracked beverage/ferment/soup/sauce turns out to matter in practice.

Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean across the whole project) and `npx eslint` on every touched file (`lib/db.ts`, `lib/alcoholCalculator.ts`, `components/AlcoholCalculator.tsx`, `components/BeverageBuilder.tsx`, `components/FermentationBuilder.tsx`, `components/SoupBuilder.tsx`, `components/SaucesBuilder.tsx`) -- all clean, zero errors, zero new warnings; a full-project `npx eslint` sweep confirmed the only remaining findings anywhere are pre-existing, unrelated noise in the separate `unified-database/` pipeline project. No `REFERENCE_DB_VERSION` bump needed -- these are local app-database migrations (the same `initializeDatabase()` pattern already used for `generic_name`/`healing_stage`/`user_condition_stages`), not a bundled reference-database change. **Not yet exercised on-device** -- worth a real, careful walkthrough (filling in Volume/ABV/Pours and confirming Quantity/Unit auto-fill and the tracked total actually shows correctly in Insights, editing a saved beverage with a calculator-tracked ingredient and confirming the calculator restores its own original inputs) before treating this as fully settled.

**The real Nutrient Ranking freeze -- a render-storm, not a slow row -- root-caused and fixed, 2026-08-12, direct report.** "I selected Insights > Nutrient Ranking > compound to rank it freezes the app for about 15 seconds and then that selector list pops in and so does the keyboard, which isn't needed and if I happen to have selected the TabHub menu it will also be displayed." A real, third instance of an already-documented bug CLASS, not a new mechanism -- `ActiveInputContext.tsx`'s own comments already record two prior real infinite-render-loop bugs (2026-07-27, Dropdown; 2026-07-27, FoodLookupView) both traced to a no-dependency-array effect calling a shared-context setState with a fresh object every render, read by something that cascades back into re-triggering it. This is a genuine, real third case of that same shape, not previously caught.

**A real, already-attempted fix for a related-but-different symptom existed in the same field's own history, confirmed via `git log`, but never actually solved this.** `components/PopoverSelect.tsx` had already been through two same-day (2026-08-11) attempts at "the Nutrient Ranking picker is slow to open" -- both focused on `FlatList`'s own `initialScrollIndex` quirk (items above a deep-list selection failing to render at all), with the final commit's own message reading "fixing the slow-open for real." That fix is real and still correct for the problem it targeted, but it was never actually confirmed on-device (no CLAUDE.md entry, no on-device confirmation anywhere), and it didn't touch the actual mechanism behind THIS report -- a genuine ~15-second freeze culminating in the popover AND the on-screen keyboard both appearing at once, with a stale TabHub tap flushing alongside them, the unmistakable signature of the whole JS thread being busy, not one row being slow to render.

**Root cause, found by reading the real execution path rather than guessing a third time**: `NutrientRankingView` (and three sibling Insights lenses -- Cooking Impact, Safe Foods, Labs) rebuilt their own `PopoverSelect` `options` array fresh on every render instead of memoizing it -- exactly the "missed optimization, not a correctness risk" gap `PopoverSelect.tsx`'s own header comment already named, except it turned out to genuinely be a correctness/performance risk after all, once combined with a second real factor: `PopoverSelect`'s own two no-dependency-array effects (`showOverlay`, `setSearchRequest`) each construct a brand-new object/element on literally every render while a picker is open, by original design, specifically so the popup and its search text always reflect live state. With the caller's own `options` prop unstable, `PopoverSelect`'s `memo()` bailout never actually held -- any unrelated re-render of the Insights screen re-rendered `PopoverSelect` too, re-firing both no-deps effects, which called `setSearchRequest`/`showOverlay` again with fresh references, re-rendering `AppKeyboard` (the one real consumer of that shared context, mounted at the app root) on every one of those ticks -- a real, high-frequency cascade, not a literal infinite loop (it does eventually settle, which is why the app recovers rather than staying stuck), but easily heavy enough to read as a genuine multi-second freeze.

**Fixed at both ends, not just the one reported field.** `app/(tabs)/insights.tsx`: `nutrientOptions`, `compoundOptions`, `categoryOptions`, and `testOptions` (Nutrient Ranking, Cooking Impact, Safe Foods, and Labs respectively -- every inline `.map()`-into-PopoverSelect-options pattern in the file, found via a direct search rather than fixing only the reported one) all now build via `useMemo`, keyed on their own real underlying source array/constant, so `PopoverSelect`'s own `memo()` bailout genuinely holds when nothing relevant changed. `components/PopoverSelect.tsx`: the `setSearchRequest` effect (the piece most directly implicated, since it's what raises the keyboard) gained a real content-equality guard -- a ref tracking what was last actually dispatched (open state, typed text, placeholder), only calling `setSearchRequest` when one of those genuinely changed, not on every incidental re-render -- a real, generic safety net for every `PopoverSelect` caller across the whole app, not just this one field, in case some future caller elsewhere reintroduces the same unmemoized-options pattern. Still fully live the moment something real does change (typing, opening, closing) -- nothing here delays or debounces a genuine update, it only skips redundant ones. The `showOverlay` effect was deliberately left as-is (harder to safely content-guard, since it carries a whole JSX tree rather than three primitives) -- with the caller-side fix already stopping the needless re-renders at the source, this effect should now only fire for genuinely relevant reasons too, as a natural consequence rather than a second, independent patch.

**Nutrient Ranking's own "Nutrient" field also had `searchable` removed outright**, a second, independent fix directly answering the other half of the report ("the keyboard, which isn't needed"): 39 real tracked nutrients is a short, plain scrollable list, not the "could definitely be longer" case search mode was originally built for (see `PopoverSelect.tsx`'s own header comment on why `searchable` exists at all). Removing it means this one field never touches `AppKeyboard`'s search row at all, closing off the whole code path most directly implicated in the freeze -- Cooking Impact's own "Nutrient / Compound" field was deliberately left `searchable`, since it wasn't named in the report and the structural fix above already covers it for the freeze risk regardless.

**A real, explicit scope note, not silently dropped**: the person's own message also described a detailed alternate layout ("place the Compound selection at the bottom slightly above the footer... have it's scrolling selection list pop in just above it on the left of the screen... Have the results appear attached to the top of the selector and extend to the bottom edge of the app header") -- offered as a possible workaround given they didn't yet know the real cause. That layout change was deliberately NOT attempted in this same pass: it's a genuinely novel, non-precedented interaction pattern for this app (nothing else pins a picker near the footer with results growing upward toward the header), and this app's own history already shows layout/positioning changes involving a `PopoverSelect`-style portal carrying real risk of their own (the LensHub "card drops in from above" saga took multiple sessions to actually root-cause). Given the freeze itself is now fixed at a real, structural level, worth confirming the underlying problem is genuinely gone before deciding whether the layout redesign is still wanted for its own ergonomic merits (not having to scroll to the top to change the ranking nutrient) rather than as a bug workaround.

Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean) and `npx eslint` (clean) on both touched files (`app/(tabs)/insights.tsx`, `components/PopoverSelect.tsx`). Metro restarted cleanly (`warning: Bundler cache is empty, rebuilding`, confirmed in its own log) so this reaches the phone via a genuinely fresh bundle, not Fast Refresh, given the significance of the change. Committed as `f09b350`, pushed to `main`. **Not yet confirmed fixed on-device** -- worth a real, careful re-test of the exact original repro (open Nutrient Ranking, tap the Nutrient field) before treating this as fully settled, especially given the field's own prior "fixing... for real" commit message that turned out not to be the whole story.

**Three new, independently-verified entries added to Basic Health's own Sleep & Health topic, 2026-08-12, direct request: research and write entries about sleep and the lymphatic system, sleep and circadian rhythm, and sleep regularity ("don't sacrifice sleep, be regular, treat sleep like an appointment you can't cancel").** Every citation independently checked via `WebSearch`/`WebFetch` before being written in, not carried over from a search summary.

`sleep-glymphatic-system` covers the brain's own real waste-clearing pathway -- the 2012 discovery of the glymphatic system (Nedergaard's lab, University of Rochester), the 2013 Xie et al. *Science* finding (PMID 24136970) that the space between brain cells expands roughly 60% during sleep, clearing amyloid-beta and other metabolic waste faster than during wakefulness, and the real, separate 2015 discovery of true meningeal lymphatic vessels (Louveau et al., *Nature*) connecting the brain's own clearance system to the body's real peripheral lymphatic network for the first time. A real, current scientific controversy is named honestly rather than smoothed over: a 2024 *Nature Neuroscience* study (Hussain et al., using a different, direct-tissue-injection measurement method) found LESS clearance during sleep and anesthesia, the opposite of the original model's prediction, with the two research groups directly disputing each other's methodology. Tiered `moderate` specifically because of this live, unresolved dispute, not because the underlying phenomenon itself is in doubt.

`sleep-circadian-rhythm-basics` covers the suprachiasmatic nucleus as the body's real master clock (roughly 20,000 neurons in the hypothalamus, reset daily by light via the retina), and cites the real, classic Scheer, Hilton, Mantzoros & Shea 2009 *PNAS* controlled-misalignment study (PMID 19255424) -- forcing healthy adults 12 hours out of their own normal sleep/wake schedule measurably reversed their cortisol rhythm, raised blood pressure and glucose, and dropped leptin within days, with real population-level shift-work data showing the same mechanism playing out chronically as elevated obesity/diabetes/cardiovascular risk. Deliberately built as the general, condition-agnostic companion to the already-existing `lifestyle-sleep-circadian` (Hashimoto's-specific TSH/cortisol framing) rather than a duplicate -- both entries now cross-link to each other.

`sleep-regularity-consistency` directly answers the "be regular, treat sleep like an appointment you can't cancel" half of the request with a real, quantified study rather than a platitude: Windred et al. 2024, *Sleep* (PMID 37738616) followed over 60,000 UK Biobank adults via real accelerometer data (10+ million hours), scored each person's own Sleep Regularity Index, and found the most sleep-regular group had a real 20-48% lower all-cause mortality risk than the least regular group over roughly 6 years, a bigger, more consistent effect in the same statistical model than sleep duration itself. Framed directly around the idea that a consistent sleep schedule is genuinely evidence-backed protective behavior, not just a tidy metaphor.

All three cross-link to each other and into the existing Sleep & Health entries (`sleep-architecture`, `sleep-tying-together`, `lifestyle-sleep-circadian`). Whole-directory verification: 1409 unique ids across the whole Digest (1406 + 3 new), zero duplicates, zero dangling `relatedIds`. `PURPLE_DIGEST_VERSION` bumped (double-checked as numerically later than the prior value). **The 2026-07-24 Wi-Fi/firewall bug, still unresolved since that date's own Next Steps entry, got a real, direct root cause and a durable fix, 2026-08-12, direct report: "the computer restarted over night and now the dev server won't connect... I thought you fixed it, so why is it still happening when the computer restarts?"** Investigated rather than assumed the old diagnosis still applied. Two real, independent findings, checked directly: (1) no Metro/Expo dev server process was running at all after the restart -- it only ever runs as a manually-launched terminal process, nothing auto-starts it on boot, so a restart genuinely does need a fresh `npm start` every time, not a bug; (2) far more consequentially, **there was no Windows Firewall rule for Node.js on this machine at all** -- not a Private-only one, not anything, confirmed via `Get-NetFirewallRule`/`Get-NetFirewallApplicationFilter` returning zero matches for node.exe or port 8081 by any name. The current network profile was checked too and came back `Private`, ruling out the original "reclassified to Public" theory as the CURRENT cause -- the real, durable gap was that nothing had ever actually granted Node.js through the firewall at all, on any profile, meaning the 2026-07-24 diagnosis was real but incomplete, and never actually confirmed fixed because it never was.

Fixed on both real halves: restarted the dev server via the real, protected `npm start` path (confirmed listening on `::8081` via `Get-NetTCPConnection`), and had the user run one elevated `New-NetFirewallRule` command (this session has no admin rights of its own, confirmed via a direct `WindowsPrincipal`/`IsInRole` check) creating a real, permanent inbound-allow rule for TCP port 8081 across all three profiles at once (Domain, Private, Public) -- deliberately covering Public too, so it doesn't matter what Windows decides to classify the home network as after any future restart or reconnect. Verified directly, not assumed: the user's own command output confirmed `Enabled: True`, `Profile: Domain, Private, Public`, `Action: Allow`, saved to `PersistentStore`; a follow-up `Get-NetFirewallRule`/`Get-NetFirewallPortFilter` query confirmed the real port/protocol filter (TCP/8081) actually attached correctly, and the dev server was still listening. **Honest gap**: the user never explicitly confirmed the phone actually reconnected after this fix (the conversation moved on to a different request) -- worth a real, direct on-device confirmation next time this comes up, rather than assuming silence means success.

**Two real Purple Digest fixes, 2026-08-12, same day, both direct requests.**

**Scroll position now resets to the top on every lens switch.** Reported directly: "Anytime I switch between the various conditions or the others that are available in the Digest, the Digest Lens I select should be scrolled to the top of it's page, not be scrolled down to whereever it was whenever it was looked at last time." Root cause, found by reading the actual `LensHub`'s own `onSelect` handler in `app/(tabs)/purple-digest.tsx`: every other piece of state it resets on a lens switch (`groupRefs`, `expandedId`, search state, `basicHealthTopicPath`) already treats it as a fresh arrival -- but the ScrollView's own native scroll offset was never touched, and swapping a ScrollView's children doesn't reset its own scroll position on its own. Fixed with one real, unanimated `scrollRef.current?.scrollTo({ y: 0, animated: false })` plus a matching `currentScrollY.current = 0` (the same ref `measureAndScrollTo`/`onScroll` elsewhere in this file already rely on, reset so nothing reads a stale value in the brief window before a real `onScroll` event would otherwise correct it) -- added directly inside the `onSelect` handler, scoped narrowly to that one reported path (not `jumpToRelated`, which already has its own real, working destination-scroll logic and wasn't part of this report).

**Every condition's own content reorganized from a fixed 4-pillar structure into 8-17 real, specific topic shelves per condition.** Reported directly: "there are tons of topics available for each condition, yet there are only Core Science, Self-Advocacy & Testing, Whole Body Effects, History & Life Stages, and Putting it all together... The user shouldn't need to dig looking for something even though they have the search utility... I want them to see something and take an interest to want to read more on their own." Investigated real content first, not designed abstractly: extracted every real entry's id/category/title across all `lib/digest/*.ts` files via a throwaway Node script (the same "parse the raw .ts source via regex, mirror the real logic, verify against real data" discipline this whole Digest build has used throughout, since `tsx`/ts-node remain unavailable in this environment) -- confirmed all 19 conditions now hold 38-48 real entries each (Hashimoto's 182), a genuinely large volume the old 4-pillar `classifyConditionPillar` function (`app/(tabs)/purple-digest.tsx`) was flattening into broad, generic buckets nobody would tap out of curiosity.

Rebuilt as `classifyConditionTopic`, a real, richer classifier checked in a deliberate priority order: id-based signals first (far more reliable than title-text keyword matching, since this app's own id conventions are deliberate and consistent) -- `-overview` forced to Core Science first (carried over unchanged from the original classifier, where this exact "an overview's own title can trip a later keyword check" bug was already found and fixed once, re-confirmed here via a real, scripted check that all 19 conditions' own `-overview` entries still land correctly); `horizon-` → "On the Horizon"; `-global-` → "Around the World"; `pregnan` → "Pregnancy & Family Planning"; `history`/`milestone` → "History & Milestones"; then a real block of Hashimoto's-only id prefixes (`gut-`, `mito-`, `healing-`, `complementary-`, `bigpicture-`, `lifestyle-`, `other-`, `labs-`, `problem-`, `nutrient-`/`additive-`/`interaction-`/`foodhistory-`) mapping to real, dedicated topic names (Gut & Microbiome, Mitochondria & Metabolism, Healing Stages, Complementary & Manual Therapies, The Big Picture, Lifestyle & Environment, Other Autoimmune Diseases) -- a harmless no-op for every other condition, whose own entries never carry these prefixes, since only Hashimoto's content is assembled from this many separate, cross-cutting source files. Everything else falls through to keyword-in-title matching, most-specific-first (Mental Health's own narrow, reliable vocabulary checked before the broader Diet/Medications/Self-Advocacy/Whole-Body nets), with Diet & Food deliberately checked ahead of Medications & Treatment so a food/drug-interaction entry (methotrexate+folate, acitretin+alcohol) lands in Diet & Food, matching this app's own food-first mission over a stricter medical-precision reading.

Verified against every real entry across all 19 conditions before shipping, not just reasoned through: every condition landed 8-17 real, non-empty topic shelves (up from a fixed 4), every singleton-sized shelf spot-checked by hand and confirmed to be a real, correctly-placed, single entry rather than a misclassification (e.g. a condition with exactly one real Mental Health finding still gets its own real "Mental Health" shelf, matching the explicit "take an interest" goal better than folding it into a vaguer bucket would). One real bug caught and fixed during this same verification pass, not shipped blind: `graves-overview`'s own title contains the word "Antibody," which would have tripped the Self-Advocacy & Testing keyword check under a naive ordering -- fixed by keeping the existing "`-overview` checked first, unconditionally" rule from the original classifier, then re-verified via a dedicated script confirming all 19 conditions' own overview entries land correctly. `groupConditionEntries`'s own returned field renamed from `pillars` to `topics` throughout (both real call sites, `shelfGroupKeyForEntry`, and every surrounding comment describing current behavior) for honesty, since "pillar" specifically implied the small, fixed structure being replaced -- historical, dated comments describing what was true at an earlier build stage were deliberately left untouched, matching this file's own established practice.

Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean across the whole project) and `npx eslint` on the one touched file (`app/(tabs)/purple-digest.tsx`) -- both clean. No `lib/digest/*.ts` content files touched, no `PURPLE_DIGEST_VERSION` bump needed -- this is a pure presentation/grouping change over already-existing, already-verified content, the same "computed, not stored" discipline the original 4-pillar version and Basic Health's own topic grouping both already established. **Not yet exercised on-device** -- both fixes are real, reasoned, and verified against real data, but neither has been seen on a real phone yet; worth a real, careful on-device check (switching between several conditions via the LensHub picker and confirming each lands at the top; opening a few different conditions and confirming the new, richer shelf rows render and scroll correctly) before treating either as fully settled.

I want them to be able to enter their harvest details into the app so it is then listed in their available food to make their meals from, so those harvested ingredients are available through the Food Builders lenses. This will be another lens on the TabHub menu, and will tie greatly into the scheduler app."** A real, substantial, cross-cutting feature, deliberately built as a genuine Phase 1 functional foundation rather than attempted all at once — every piece named below is real and working, with the deliberately-deferred pieces named honestly rather than silently skipped.

**A new tab, Garden, with its own real identity color and icon.** `constants/colors.ts` gained `tabGarden` (`#F1ACF6`, hue 296°, the real widest remaining hue gap in the whole palette — 68° between Purple Digest at 262 and Profile at 330 — computed and contrast-verified at 3.96:1 against `menuSurface`, the same discipline every other tab color in this palette has been held to). `IRIDESCENT_PALETTE`'s own fixed-length tuple type widened from 8 to 9 stops to include it — every real consumer (`ScreenHeader`, `ScreenBackground`, `IridescentRingCircle`) hands the whole array straight to a `LinearGradient`'s own `colors` prop with no fixed-position destructuring anywhere, confirmed by reading all three before touching the type, so widening it was safe. `constants/tabs.ts`'s `TAB_ROUTES` gained a real 9th entry (`path: '/garden'`, icon `'leaf'`), appended last per the same precedent Purple Digest itself set 2026-08-05, so no other tab's own swipe-adjacency changed. `app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx` registered a real `<Tabs.Screen name="garden">`.

**A real, general fix to TabHub's own row/centering math, not a one-off patch.** `TabHub.tsx`'s "Info centered alone on its own final row" layout used to be a single hardcoded blank spacer, correct only for the specific case of exactly 9 real items (8 tabs + Profile) landing on an exact multiple of 3. Adding Garden as a 9th tab (10 items + Profile before Info) broke that exact assumption — traced by hand-tracing the real flexbox item order before touching anything, not guessed. Replaced with real, computed constants (`CARD_GRID_COLUMNS`, `ITEMS_BEFORE_INFO`, `INFO_ROW_PAD_COUNT`, `INFO_BLANK_SPACER_COUNT`, `CARD_ROW_COUNT`) deriving the correct number of blank spacers and total row count from `TAB_ROUTES.length` directly, verified by hand against both the old 8-tab case (reproduces the original single-spacer, 4-row layout exactly) and the new 9-tab case (3 spacers, 5 rows) before shipping — so a future 10th tab won't need this same fix redone by hand.

**Real, standing database infrastructure**: four new local app tables in `lib/db.ts` (`garden_plots`, `garden_plantings`, `garden_harvests`, `garden_task_links`), plus a full real CRUD layer (`createGardenPlot`/`listGardenPlots`/`updateGardenPlot`/`archiveGardenPlot`/`deleteGardenPlot`, the same shape for plantings, and `recordGardenHarvest`/`listGardenHarvests`/`listAvailableHarvests`/`recordHarvestUsage`/`deleteGardenHarvest`). A real, deliberate design choice: `garden_plantings`/`garden_harvests` both store a genuine `food_id`/`source` pair pointing straight into the same bundled reference database every Food builder already reads from — a harvested tomato is the identical real reference-database row (and identical real nutrition/6-DFF scoring) as any other tomato, never a second, separate "garden food" concept. `user_profile` gained a real `growing_zone` column (via the established `PRAGMA table_info` + conditional `ALTER TABLE` migration pattern) and a matching `growingZone` field on `UserProfile`/`getUserProfile`/`setUserProfile`.

**A real, if deliberately basic, Scheduler tie-in**, directly answering "will tie greatly into the scheduler app": `insertScheduleSeries`'s own `itemType` union (previously `'meal' | 'supplement' | 'prescription' | 'appointment'`) widened to include `'garden'`, reusing the exact same real repeat/rolling-window machinery every other schedule item already gets rather than a second, parallel mechanism — a garden task genuinely can repeat daily/weekly the same way a supplement dose does. `scheduleGardenTask()` creates a real `schedule_items` row plus a `garden_task_links` row (tracing it back to the real plot/planting it's about), and `listUpcomingGardenTasks()` reads it straight back. **A real, honest scope limit, not an oversight**: every existing Schedule lens (Meals/Supplements/Prescriptions/Appointments) queries its own `item_type` explicitly rather than rendering any `item_type` generically, so a `'garden'` row doesn't appear inside the Schedules tab's own UI yet — the Garden tab's own "Upcoming Garden Tasks" list (reading the identical real row back) is the real, working way to see it for now; a dedicated Schedule-side lens is a real, named Phase 2 item.

**A real, new `app/(tabs)/garden.tsx` screen**, following the exact same `SwipeableTabScreen` → `GatedTabContent` → `LensHub` architecture `app/(tabs)/food.tsx` already established, with three real, working lenses. **My Zone**: a real, functional USDA Plant Hardiness Zone picker (zones 1a-13b, the same real framework `lib/digest/homeGardening.ts`'s own `garden-understanding-your-zone` entry already establishes) writing to the shared `growingZone` profile field, cross-referencing the real, already-published Digest zone-band content (a new, shared `lib/gardenZones.ts` — `USDA_ZONES`/`zoneBandInfo()` — used by both this screen and Profile's own mirrored field, so neither drifts out of sync; zone 10's own real overlap between the Digest's "warm" and "tropical/subtropical" entries is handled honestly, showing both, rather than picking one arbitrarily). **Plots & Plantings**: real create/list/expand/archive/delete for plots, with an embedded `FoodLookup` (`showNutrients={false}`) to add a real planting tied to a real reference food. **Harvest Log**: the same embedded `FoodLookup` to log what was actually picked, real quantity/unit entry via `PopoverSelect` (matching this app's own standing "PopoverSelect over a raw keyboard" convention), a real remaining-inventory list, and the real "Add a Garden Task" mini-form feeding `scheduleGardenTask`. Uses `useAutoOpenLensHubSignal()`, the same shared hook every other tab's own LensHub already relies on for "opened directly from TabHub" auto-open behavior — no TabHub-side special-casing was needed for this to work.

**The core "harvested ingredients are available through the Food Builders lenses" request, wired for real into the shared `FoodLookup.tsx`** every one of the 11 Food builders already uses. A new "From Your Harvest" section (real, unused inventory only — `listAvailableHarvests()`, `quantity_remaining > 0`) surfaces above the ordinary Category step whenever a real `onFoodResolved` callback is present and `showNutrients` is false — i.e., every builder's own connected picker, not Insights' general-purpose lookup lens, a real, deliberate, honestly-scoped-and-stated boundary rather than an unstated gap. Tapping a harvest resolves it straight into a real `ResolvedFoodSelection` via `getFoodIdentity(foodId, source)` — the exact same "reconstruct a full selection from a stored foodId/source" mechanism SideBuilder's own Edit flow already relies on, not a second, separate resolution path — bypassing Category/Type/Food/Prep entirely, since the harvest record already names one concrete row. **A real, honest, deliberate scope limit, named directly rather than silently left half-wired**: drawing down a harvest's own `quantity_remaining` as it's actually consumed (`recordHarvestUsage`, already built and ready) is NOT yet wired into any of the 11 builders' own ingredient-save step — doing so correctly across all 11 (each with its own internal architecture, some ~2,000 lines per CLAUDE.md's own build history) without real risk of double-decrementing on an edit or misattributing a later food swap is genuine, separate Phase 2 work, not attempted in this same pass. Selecting real harvest food identity, with real nutrition/6-DFF scoring, is fully real and working today; usage tracking against it is not yet.

**A real, focused first Digest research batch (Part B of the same request), 5 new entries in `lib/digest/homeGardening.ts`, every citation independently verified via WebSearch/WebFetch before being written in.** Directly answers "encourage people to put carbon into the ground": `garden-carbon-in-the-ground` cites a real, rigorous 19-year UC Davis Russell Ranch field trial (Global Change Biology) finding compost PLUS cover crops together — neither alone — raised soil carbon 12.6% over the study period (about 0.7%/year, ahead of the international "4 per 1000" target already covered in Earth Matters, cross-linked directly). Directly answers "we should all be growing everything we can no matter how small": `garden-grow-what-you-can-however-small` cites a real, striking, verified WWII statistic (National WWII Museum, citing real USDA figures via a 1943 Roosevelt fireside chat) — by 1944, more than 20 million ordinary, mostly small American home "victory gardens" together supplied 42% of the country's entire vegetable supply, real concrete proof that small, individually modest gardens genuinely add up at scale. The first real installment of the much larger indoor-growing-equipment research also requested: `garden-indoor-growing-methods-overview` (a real, honest comparison of soil/hydroponic/aeroponic growing, with real, cited yield/water-use figures and their real tradeoffs, not a claim that one is simply "better"), `garden-led-grow-lights-photoperiod` (a real, controlled dwarf-tomato LED study — 300/500/700 μmol/m²/s tested — finding the highest intensity produced the most growth but the LOWEST tested intensity was the most energy-efficient per unit of growth, a real, honest tradeoff rather than a simple "more light is better" claim, with a real `DigestChart`), and `garden-water-quality-filtration` (a real, Extension-sourced, honest answer: ordinary tap water is typically fine for soil growing per the EPA/University of Nebraska Extension, but hydroponic/aeroponic systems and young seedlings are the real, genuine exception, with a real, useful chlorine-vs-chloramine distinction most general advice glosses over). The closing `garden-tying-together` synthesis entry was updated in place to fold in all five, not left describing only the prior batches.

**Explicitly, honestly NOT covered in this same pass, named directly rather than silently dropped** (both this file's own header comment and the CLAUDE.md entry here say so): grow tents/airflow equipment specifics, real plant-nutrient forms and dosing, full crop life-cycle growing/maintenance guidance, composting kitchen scraps in more depth than the existing `garden-composting-at-home` entry already covers, and atmospheric-water-harvesting/rainwater-harvesting (collection, filtration, safe storage duration, non-chemical preservation) — all real, standing next steps for a future continuation of this same research batch, matching the exact "real, incremental, never falsely claimed complete" discipline this whole Digest has run on throughout its build history.

Whole-directory verification: 1,426 unique ids across the whole Digest, zero duplicates, zero dangling `relatedIds`. `PURPLE_DIGEST_VERSION` bumped (double-checked as numerically later than the prior value, given this project's own documented history of real system-clock oscillation). `REFERENCE_DB_VERSION` was NOT bumped — every new table this pass is a real, local-only app table created via the existing `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` migration pattern, not part of the bundled reference database. Verified via `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean across the whole project) and `npx eslint` on every touched/new file (`app/(tabs)/garden.tsx`, `app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx`, `app/profile.tsx`, `components/FoodLookup.tsx`, `components/TabHub.tsx`, `constants/colors.ts`, `constants/tabs.ts`, `lib/db.ts`, `lib/gardenZones.ts`, `lib/digest/homeGardening.ts`, `lib/digest/index.ts`) — all clean, zero errors, zero new warnings (every pre-existing `app/profile.tsx` finding independently re-confirmed unrelated to this pass's own edits). **Not yet exercised on-device** — this is real, substantial new interaction surface (a new tab, a new cross-tab data flow into every Food builder, a new Scheduler tie-in) built entirely this session with no on-device confirmation yet; worth a real, careful walkthrough (setting a zone in both Profile and the Garden tab and confirming they stay in sync, creating a plot and a planting, logging a harvest, confirming it shows up as "From Your Harvest" in a real builder like Side Builder, and creating a garden task and seeing it in the Garden tab's own Upcoming list) before treating any of it as fully settled.

**A real, confirmed on-device crash from the Garden tab build above was root-caused and fixed the same day, 2026-08-13, direct report (a shared screenshot): `Call to function 'NativeDatabase.prepareAsync' has been rejected. → Caused by: java.lang.NullPointerException`.** Diagnosed via `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`, the project's own established method — the real, live Metro/Expo dev server had been running continuously since well before that day's real schema changes (the new `garden_plots`/`garden_plantings`/`garden_harvests`/`garden_task_links` tables and the `user_profile.growing_zone` column) were ever written, so the app was reaching for tables a stale bundle had no idea existed. Fixed by killing the entire stale process tree and restarting cleanly via the protected `npm start -- --clear` path, confirmed via a genuine "Bundler cache is empty, rebuilding" log line — no code change needed, matching this project's own long-documented "check Metro's own process age before re-guessing the code" discipline. **Confirmed fixed by the person directly**: "Confirmed fixed, works now."

**Four more real, direct requests the same day, all four completed in one pass.** Quoted in full: *"From the Digest tab, move Earth Matters and Home Gardening up to the top with Basic Health and Search All. Keep Search All in the top left, followed by Basic Health, then Earth Matters, then Gardening (Renamed from Home Gardening), and then the conditions in alphabetical order with the ones selected in the profile as their conditions being at the top of the conditions in alphabetical order within their own little group. On the TabHub menu, let's try using 'Forest Green' (Hex #228B22) for the color of the Garden icon and LensHub lenses and line colors. Move the Info icon up one row so it is in the middle spot, just to the right of the Profile icon."*

1. **Purple Digest's own LensHub picker reordered.** `app/(tabs)/purple-digest.tsx`'s `orderedCategoryMetas` construction rewritten: Search All stays hardcoded first (untouched, outside this whole array), then a real, fixed lookup for `basicHealthMeta`/`earthMattersMeta`/`gardeningMeta` (each exists exactly once, no sorting needed), then every OTHER real category (all 19 conditions, Hashimoto's included — no longer hardcoded to a fixed second position) split into the person's own selected conditions and everything else, each block independently sorted alphabetically by its own real display `.label` via `.localeCompare()` rather than hand-ordered, so this stays correct automatically if a condition's name or the roster itself ever changes. The existing `★` pinned-condition marker logic (excluding Basic Health and Hashimoto's from the star) is a separate, still-valid mechanism and was deliberately left untouched.

3. **Garden's tab color changed from the computed hue-spread pastel (`#F1ACF6`) to a deliberately chosen Forest Green (`#228B22`)**, per direct request — a real, deliberate departure from the rest of `constants/colors.ts`'s own rigorously engineered palette, not another member of it. Flows automatically into everywhere `colors.tabGarden` is already read: the Garden tab's own `LensHub` (its 3 real lens tiles), TabHub's Garden icon, and the shared `IRIDESCENT_PALETTE` divider-line shimmer (all 9 tabs' colors, feeding the header/footer line animation — the real "line colors" named in the request) — no code changes needed at any of those three consumer sites, only the one source value. **A real, honest tradeoff computed and stated directly in the code's own comment, not silently glossed over**: Forest Green's own real WCAG contrast ratio against `colors.menuSurface` (`#545A63`) comes out to roughly 1.6:1 — well below the 3:1 floor every OTHER tab color in this palette is verified to clear. Left as the person's own explicit, named choice rather than silently adjusted or reverted, flagged for a real on-device look and a possible second pass if it reads as genuinely hard to see once actually seen.
4. **TabHub's Info tile repositioned**, `components/TabHub.tsx`. The `INFO_ROW_PAD_COUNT`/`INFO_BLANK_SPACER_COUNT` blank-spacer machinery (built earlier the same day specifically to force Info onto its own dedicated, centered final row) was removed entirely, along with its matching spacer-rendering `.map()` block in the JSX — Info now renders immediately after Profile with zero spacers. With 9 real tabs, Profile (item index 9, 0-indexed) already lands in column 0 of its own row (`9 % 3 = 0`); the very next item, Info, therefore falls naturally into column 1, the middle slot of that SAME row, immediately to Profile's right — exactly the "middle spot, just to the right of the Profile icon" the request describes, needing zero forced padding at all once Info is simply let to fall where it naturally would. `CARD_ROW_COUNT` recomputed accordingly (`Math.ceil((ITEMS_BEFORE_INFO + 1) / CARD_GRID_COLUMNS)`, 5 rows → 4).
